items.title: Michael Baidoo returns from injury to score in Plymouth win over Alvechurch
items.description: Ghanaian midfielder Michael Baidoo made his injury return for Plymouth Argyle in their heavy win over Alvechurch in the English FA Cup on Saturday. Baidoo returned with a bang as he scored in his side’s 4-0 hammering of the lower-tier side in the cup competition. The midfielder had been out of action since August, when he came off injured after 30 minutes in the friendly against Bristol City following an injury. The 27-year-old had missed the last 18 games of his club due to his time on the sidelines. However, he made a comeback in the FA Cup first-round victory, which sees them advance into the next stage of th competition. Baidoo was introduced into the game in the 61st minute of the encounter and scored 17 minutes later to make it 3-0 after Will Evans’ second half double. The Ghanaian will be hoping to get more game time following his return from injury.

items.title: Réforme de la santé : 6.000 recrutements, de nouveaux CHU et le recours aux médecins étrangers
items.description: Le ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale entend accélérer la réforme du système de santé marocain, en misant sur le renforcement des ressources humaines, la modernisation des infrastructures hospitalières et l’amélioration de l’accès aux soins. Présentant le projet de budget sectoriel de son département pour 2027 devant la Commission des secteurs sociaux de la Chambre des représentants, le ministre Youns Bjijou a annoncé une série de mesures visant à accélérer la réalisation des projets, à garantir la qualité et la continuité des soins et à réduire les délais d’accès aux traitements. Parmi les principales mesures figure un plan de recrutement de 6.000 infirmiers et techniciens de santé entre novembre 2026 et février 2027. Selon un document de la Direction des ressources humaines du ministère, cette opération vise à intégrer les diplômés des Instituts supérieurs des professions infirmières et techniques de santé (ISPITS) encore en attente de recrutement. Le calendrier prévoit un concours le dimanche 22 novembre, portant sur 2.094 postes, puis l’ouverture de 906 postes dans le cadre des concours des groupements sanitaires territoriaux en décembre. À ces recrutements s’ajouteront 3.000 postes supplémentaires en février 2027. Les 906 postes destinés aux groupements sanitaires territoriaux seront répartis entre trois régions : Rabat-Salé-Kénitra, avec 450 postes, Fès-Meknès, avec 250 postes, et Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma, avec 206 postes. Les 2.094 postes relevant du concours organisé par le ministère concerneront six régions. L’Oriental arrive en tête avec 594 postes, suivi de Béni Mellal-Khénifra, avec 550 postes, et de Marrakech-Safi, avec 500 postes. Guelmim-Oued Noun bénéficiera de 300 postes, Drâa-Tafilalet de 100 postes et Dakhla-Oued Eddahab de 50 postes. Cette programmation vise à résorber la situation de 5.933 diplômés des ISPITS en attente d’intégration, selon les statistiques d’octobre 2026. Elle intervient après le recrutement de 2.467 diplômés en juin et juillet derniers, sur un total de 8.400 personnes ciblées. D’après le document, les opérations prévues entre novembre 2026 et février 2027 devraient permettre d’intégrer l’ensemble des diplômés en attente et de régler définitivement cette situation à l’horizon février 2027. Le ministère devra toutefois anticiper l’arrivée de nouvelles promotions. Environ 8.000 cadres devraient sortir des ISPITS en 2027, contre 7.000 en 2026. Pour préparer leur intégration, des commissions conjointes réunissant, à partir d’avril 2027, la Direction des ressources humaines, les groupements sanitaires territoriaux, les directions de la santé et de la protection sociale ainsi que les ISPITS seront chargées d’établir les estimations du nombre de diplômés et de planifier leur recrutement. Des infrastructures hospitalières à renforcer Au-delà des recrutements, le ministre a présenté les grandes orientations de la réforme, qui s’articulera autour de sept priorités interdépendantes, fondées sur les choix du programme gouvernemental. L’objectif est de produire des effets tangibles sur le fonctionnement du système de santé et la qualité des prestations, notamment en adaptant l’offre de soins aux besoins de la population. Youns Bjijou a annoncé la transformation des centres hospitaliers provinciaux de Settat et de Kénitra en centres hospitaliers universitaires (CHU). Cette évolution doit permettre de rapprocher les soins de niveau tertiaire des habitants des deux provinces, tout en offrant des espaces de formation clinique et de stages hospitaliers aux étudiants des deux facultés de médecine créées dans ces villes. Un nouveau CHU sera également construit à Casablanca, avec une « capacité d’accueil importante », afin de répondre aux besoins de la population de la région et à la pression démographique qu’elle connaît. Le ministre a insisté sur la nécessité de ne pas limiter la politique d’investissement à la construction et à la programmation des projets. Leur réussite, a-t-il expliqué, dépendra de la capacité des établissements à entrer effectivement en service et à disposer des ressources humaines, des médicaments, des équipements et des spécialités nécessaires pour assurer la continuité et la qualité des soins. Le département prévoit ainsi de mettre en place un système de maintenance préventive et anticipative, reposant sur le suivi régulier de l’état technique des infrastructures et des équipements sanitaires. Ce dispositif permettra notamment d’évaluer leur disponibilité, leurs taux d’utilisation et les délais nécessaires à leur réparation. Les professionnels de santé au cœur de la réforme Le renforcement des ressources humaines constitue, selon le ministre, un autre pilier de la réforme. Les efforts porteront sur l’amélioration des conditions d’exercice, le renforcement de l’attractivité du secteur, la motivation des personnels, le développement des compétences et des parcours professionnels, ainsi que sur une répartition plus équilibrée des ressources humaines en fonction des besoins des régions et des établissements. « Si nécessaire, nous mobiliserons les compétences marocaines résidant à l’étranger et nous ouvrirons, de manière organisée, le secteur aux compétences étrangères dans les spécialités confrontées à des pénuries, considérant cette démarche comme un mécanisme complémentaire pour renforcer le capital humain national », a déclaré Youns Bjijou. Le dialogue social, aux niveaux national et territorial, restera également un cadre de suivi des mesures convenues et de concertation sur les moyens d’améliorer les conditions d’exercice des professionnels. Sur le plan des effectifs, le document de la Direction des ressources humaines fait état d’une progression importante des postes budgétaires consacrés au recrutement des infirmiers et techniciens de santé. Ceux-ci sont passés de 2.095 en 2023 à 4.947 en 2026, sur un total de 8.000 postes budgétaires alloués au ministère cette année. Cette évolution représente une hausse de 136 % par rapport à 2023. Réduire les délais d’attente et le coût des soins La réforme doit également s’attacher à simplifier le parcours des patients dans les établissements de santé, à réduire les délais d’attente et à améliorer les services d’urgence et d’aide médicale urgente. Le ministère prévoit, à cet effet, de généraliser et d’améliorer les services d’accueil et d’orientation, de mettre en place des systèmes locaux et régionaux de prise de rendez-vous médicaux et d’adopter une gestion régionale intégrée des lits hospitaliers. Il entend également élargir progressivement le service d’aide médicale urgente accessible via le numéro national unifié 141. Le coût des soins constitue un autre enjeu de la réforme. Le ministre a annoncé que son département contribuerait « activement » à la révision de la tarification nationale de référence pour le remboursement des frais de soins, dans le cadre des compétences de la Haute Autorité de santé et en tenant compte de la pérennité des régimes de couverture. « La valeur de l’assurance maladie ne s’accomplit pas pleinement si le coût des soins demeure un obstacle à leur accès ou une cause de leur report », a-t-il souligné. Le programme gouvernemental prévoit, dans ce cadre, l’achèvement de la généralisation d’une couverture sanitaire universelle et effective, l’augmentation à 50 % de la part des établissements publics de santé dans les dépenses de l’assurance maladie obligatoire de base à l’horizon 2031, ainsi que l’atteinte d’un ratio de 35 professionnels de santé pour 10.000 habitants. Une enveloppe budgétaire de 45,36 milliards de dirhams Pour soutenir ces différents chantiers, le projet de budget sectoriel du ministère de la Santé pour 2027 prévoit une enveloppe globale d’environ 45,36 milliards de dirhams, soit près de 3 milliards de dirhams supplémentaires par rapport à 2026. Cette progression représente une hausse de 7,08 %. Les crédits de paiement destinés à l’investissement s’élèvent à environ 14,5 milliards de dirhams, tandis que les crédits d’engagement atteignent près de 16,1 milliards de dirhams. Ces allocations doivent permettre de poursuivre le financement des projets structurants et d’assurer la continuité de leur réalisation. Le projet prévoit également une enveloppe de 2 milliards de dirhams pour le compte spécial de la Pharmacie centrale, ainsi que la création de 8.000 nouveaux postes budgétaires destinés à répondre aux besoins du système de santé en ressources humaines. Le ministre a enfin annoncé que le budget proposé serait renforcé par des crédits supplémentaires, dont le montant sera communiqué après l’achèvement des vérifications techniques en cours. Cette décision, a-t-il précisé, traduit la priorité accordée par le gouvernement à la réforme du système de santé et sa volonté de mobiliser les ressources nécessaires pour accélérer la mise en œuvre des projets ayant un impact direct sur les citoyens. The post Réforme de la santé : 6.000 recrutements, de nouveaux CHU et le recours aux médecins étrangers appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Politician and businessman Kofi Wayo passes on at 71
items.description: Ghanaian politician and businessman Charles Eric Kofi Wayo, popularly known as Kofi Wayo or ‘Chuck’, has died at the age of 71. A death announcement circulated on Saturday, November 7, 2026, indicated that he passed away in the early hours of the day at Nyaho Clinic in Accra. Kofi Wayo, who resided in East Legon, was widely known for his outspoken views on national politics and his criticism of successive governments. Although he never held high political office, he established himself as a distinctive voice in Ghana’s political landscape, attracting public attention through his blunt commentary on governance, corruption and the country’s economic direction. He also ventured into active party politics, founding the United Renaissance Party (URP) after engagements with other political parties. His unconventional style and willingness to challenge political leaders across the political divide made him a recognisable figure in Ghanaian public discourse. His death marks the passing of a public figure whose political views and outspoken approach often generated considerable debate. The family is yet to announce funeral arrangements. Political background Kofi Wayo first gained national attention in the early 2000s through his outspoken criticism of the government of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and later became associated with the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP). He contested the Ayawaso East parliamentary seat on the NPP ticket in the 2000 general elections but lost to the incumbent. His relationship with the NPP became strained after the party assumed office in 2001, as he frequently criticised the Kufuor administration over governance and economic management. He subsequently broke away from the party, associated with the People’s National Convention (PNC) and later established the United Renaissance Party (URP), for which he served as founder and leader. Mr Wayo also expressed interest in contesting the presidency and was endorsed as the URP’s presidential candidate in 2012. Beyond politics, he advocated agricultural development and supported farmers through the distribution of farming tools, including cutlasses. In 2017, he announced his intention to leave active politics and focus on farming, saying he wanted to support rural farmers. His political career was marked by outspoken criticism of successive governments, frequent media appearances and an unconventional approach to political activism.

items.title: Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has hit back at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and others criticising his administration over hardship and hunger, accusing them of contributing to the problems he inherited. Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Responding to those raising concerns about hunger, Tinubu said his administration was working to address the problems left behind by previous governments. “Those people talking of hunger, I’m cleaning the mess they created. Atiku was one of them,” Tinubu said. He then questioned how Atiku, who served as vice president and was involved in economic affairs during the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, was able to establish a university while in office. “Ask him how he built a university while in office as vice president in charge of our economy. Who built the university for him? It’s your money. It’s your effort,” he said. He further questioned Atiku’s moral standing to criticise his administration, describing him as a man lacking the integrity and ethical standards required for public office. Tinubu also expressed appreciation to Rivers residents for the support they gave him during the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his emergence as president. “Thank you for the last election. In 2022, 2023, I looked very hopeless, but you trooped out to support me and gave me the mandate,” Tinubu said. “I’m seeking a second term because you believe in me and that I care for you,” he said. items.title: Pakistani startup led by Nust graduate wins award at Silicon Valley summit
items.description: Pakistani startup RLabs has won the best startup award at the Silicon Valley November Summit in California, with the government on Saturday hailing the achievement as showcasing the “growing strength of our startup ecosystem”. RLabs, a Pakistani startup incubated at the National Incubation Centre for Aerospace Technologies (Nicat) and led by Harris Ahmed, won the ‘GOAL Startup Award’ at the summit . The event, held from Nov 2 to Nov 5, was organised by Plug and Play , an innovation platform and a venture capital firm. RLabs was among 18 startups from around the world that “earned the incredible opportunity to pitch their idea” at the summit under Plug and Play’s Global Overseas Acceleration & Learning (GOAL) programme. “Had the opportunity to present our work on XR (extended reality) simulators, synthetic data and machine training on a platform that brought together more than 3,000 attendees, including founders, venture capitalists, corporate executives, innovation leaders, and government partners,” Ahmed wrote on his LinkedIn account, sharing a photo of him posing with the award. Ahmed, a 2018 graduate of the National University of Sciences and Technology (Nust) as per his profile, said he “spent the last decade teaching humans how to operate complex machines in XR”. “Now we use the same human experience to train machine instincts. (Launching in the US soon),” he added. Ahmed noted that the summit centred on artificial intelligence (AI) and deep tech, featuring live demonstrations and pitches from over 300 startups across more than 20 industry programmes. According to Nicat , RLabs had been training a proprietary Large Language Model to “power a modular, cross-platform simulation engine that cuts development time by 75 per cent”. In a statement , also posted by the government’s official X account, IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja wrote: “From Pakistan to Silicon Valley — a proud moment for our nation!” She termed the achievement a “moment of immense pride” for her ministry and tech innovation arm Ignite , reflecting the “extraordinary potential of Pakistani talent and the growing strength of our startup ecosystem”. “Seeing our homegrown startups earn international recognition reinforces our commitment to nurturing innovation, creating global opportunities, and empowering the next generation of Pakistani entrepreneurs,” the minister said. She reaffirmed the government’s vision: “Pakistani startups should not just compete globally, but help shape the future of technology.” “Congratulations to Harris Ahmed and the entire RLabs team for making Pakistan proud. May this be one of many more success stories that take our green flag to new heights!” the statement added. On Oct 10, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formally inaugurated the newly renamed Daanish IT Park (National Technology Park), hailing the country’s first national technology facility as a crucial milestone for Pakistan’s rapid economic progress and prosperity. He noted that the state-of-the-art facility brings incubation centres, innovation hubs, small and medium enterprises, startups, and industry leaders together under one roof. The World Bank — under the “Pakistan Entrepr­eneurship and Private In­­v­­estment Catalyst Proj­ect” expected to be approved by its executive board in early 2027 — would help the government establish and capitalise a $50 million Fund of Funds (FoF) to catalyse Pakistan’s nascent innovation and venture capital ecosystem. Earlier this year, co-founders of Singapore-based Plouton AI secured a spot in the ‘finance and venture capital’ category of the Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia list. The venture, co-founded by Muhammad Furqan Karim Kidwai and Sarfraz Shahid Hussain, was described as an “agentic automation platform that helps midmarket companies automate finance workflows”.

items.title: Tinubu: Yari sets 2.3m votes target for Rivers APC
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Sen. Abdulaziz Yari, on Saturday set a target of 2.3 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers state in the January 16 election. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Yari said the party would mobilize its supporters to achieve the feat. “The message here, we are looking for at least nothing less than 2.3 million votes,” he said. He asked the crowd to raise their hands if they were ready to support the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to deliver Tinubu at that figure. Yari said the figure was within reach, citing voter data he obtained from the coalition’s leaders in the state. “Out of 3.3 million voters registered and about 2.8 million PVCs collected, we should be aiming at nothing less than 2.3 million,” he said. He told the President that Rivers was one of the states from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent, by God’s grace.” Yari also took aim at the opposition, saying those seeking power had themselves been in government without achieving anything tangible. “From Atiku, to Peter Obi, to Amaechi, down to vice president Atiku Abubakar. He was elected as a governor before becoming a vice president,” he said. The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, said Rivers was the only state in the South-South that Tinubu won convincingly in 2023, and that the state was ready to repeat the feat. He equally added that under Tinubu, Nigeria now gets more revenue from taxation than from crude oil. National Chairman of the APC, Nentawe Yilwatda, described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria.” “Here, we have the numbers. Here, we have the voters,” he said of Rivers. Senator Magnus Abe, who spoke on behalf of Rivers stakeholders, defended the Rainbow Coalition, whose members, he said, have diverse interests but “whose main interest is to return the president to power.” Abe said he was surprised to hear some party members talking down on the coalition. items.title: Florence Beaugé : « En France, on n’est pas fier du passé en Algérie »
items.description: Ancienne journaliste au journal Le Monde, Florence Beaugé a pris part au Salon international du livre d’Alger (SILA 2026, 29 octobre – 7 octobre) pour y dédicacer son livre « Algérie une guerre sans gloire » publié aux éditions Barzakh. Lors d’une rencontre, l’écrivaine et journaliste française a accordé une interview à TSA. Vous êtes au Sila 2026 pour présenter votre ouvrage « Algérie, une guerre sans gloire ». Pouvez-vous nous parler de ce livre ? Florence Beaugé : C’est un livre que j’ai porté longtemps en moi, et dont la première édition date de 2005 mais ce qu’il y a de terrible, c’est qu’il n’a pas pris une ride. Cela veut dire que les rapports entre la France et l’Algérie sont toujours aussi durs, aussi difficiles et dans l’incompréhension mutuelle depuis plus de 20 ans. Les éditions Barzakh l’ont réédité cette année mais en version augmentée. Il y a de nouvelles révélations, ainsi que les coulisses de l’enquête. C’est un livre qui porte sur la torture pendant la guerre d’indépendance algérienne mais aussi sur ce qu’est le métier de journaliste. Par exemple, j’ai eu un procès avec Jean Marie Le Pen, j’ai dénoncé le général Schmitt qui était le tortionnaire en chef de l’école Sarrouy, appelée aujourd’hui Ourida Meddad. Toutes ces atrocités, qu’on connaissait déjà, étaient tombées en désuétude et il y a eu un retour de mémoire en 2000 grâce à Louisette Ighilahriz. J’avais publié un article sur elle et il a fait la Une du Monde en juin 2000. À partir de là, j’ai fait parler Massu et c’est lui qui a identifié le sauveur d’Ighilahriz alors qu’elle était retenue au siège de la 10ème division parachutiste. Ensuite j’ai eu les dénégations de Bigeard, puis les aveux d’Aussaresses. J’ai continué sur la lancée pour raconter ce qu’il s’est passé en France, pendant la guerre d’indépendance et qu’on voulait ignorer. Ceux qui ont lu « La Gangrène » de Bachir Boumaza ou « La Question » d’Henri Alleg pouvaient très bien être au courant mais en France on n’est pas très fier de ce passé. On a du mal à le regarder en face. Vous avez été journaliste au Monde, où vous étiez notamment chargée de couvrir l’Algérie. Qu’est-ce qui a éveillé votre intérêt pour la guerre d’Algérie ? Florence Beaugé : Oui c’était durant les années Bouteflika. J’étais supposée couvrir uniquement l’actualité du jour, mais j’ai travaillé en parallèle, tout le temps, sur la guerre d’indépendance algérienne, parce que celle-ci était tellement mêlée à la vie de vos parents, grands-parents et vos familles, qu’elle revenait tout le temps dans les conversations. Je me suis rendue compte que je ne connaissais presque rien de la guerre d’indépendance algérienne et qu’il était grand temps que moi-même je m’informe. C’est votre première participation au Salon international du livre d’Alger. Quelles sont vos impressions ? Florence Beaugé : C’est ma première participation mais cela fait longtemps que j’entends parler du SILA. Je suis à la fois honorée et gratifiée de venir ici. Je suis émerveillée de voir tous ces gens, l’activité, la joie et l’intérêt parce qu’au moment où on dit qu’il n’y a plus de lecteurs – en France aussi on s’en alarme beaucoup-, je me dis que c’est touchant et impressionnant. Je vois beaucoup de jeunes, à l’heure de l’intelligence artificielle où on se dit que la lecture ne présente plus d’attrait, eh bien ce salon démontre l’inverse. L’article Florence Beaugé : « En France, on n’est pas fier du passé en Algérie » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
items.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. items.title: Alfred Woyome files nomination to contest NDC National Vice Chairmanship
items.description: Businessman and National Democratic Congress (NDC) member, Alfred Agbesi Woyome, has filed his nomination to contest the position of National Vice Chairperson of the party. His nomination was submitted by former Deputy National Women’s Organiser of the NDC, Dr Catherine Deynu, who said Mr Woyome’s ambition was to strengthen the party’s organisational structures and build its capacity ahead of future elections. She said he intended to prioritise the empowerment of party members, particularly at the grassroots and constituency levels, to help sustain the NDC’s electoral fortunes. According to Dr Deynu, Mr Woyome’s contributions to the party over the years had positioned him to play a greater role in consolidating its structures and improving its organisational capacity. “Many people can attest to these facts. He has done a lot for the party, and this is the time for him to be at the helm of affairs to ensure that our grassroots members are empowered and that those at the constituency level have their capacity built. He can also help build a strong party that will sustain electoral victories for years to come,” she told Accra-based Citi FM. Dr Deynu added that Mr Woyome’s vision also included prioritising sustainable job creation as part of efforts to strengthen the party and improve the capacity of its members. The NDC is scheduled to elect its national executives at its National Delegates Congress on Saturday, December 19, 2026, as part of its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections.

items.title: Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths to collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the 2027 general elections, saying the outcome of the poll will have a direct bearing on their future. Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Addressing the youths at the rally, the president said the election should not be viewed as being about his personal ambition but about determining the future of the younger generation. “To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said. Tinubu urged Nigerians who were yet to collect their PVCs to do so, describing the voter card as the means through which citizens could determine the country’s leadership. “It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. “I take God, beg you,” he said. The president also identified economic development as a key tool for young Nigerians to overcome poverty, saying his administration was working to improve the economy and ensure that prosperity was widely shared. He said previous administrations had left behind unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of naira, adding that his government was clearing the outstanding obligations. “The people that governed before left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” Tinubu said. He listed retired professionals, including engineers, welders, and teachers, among those benefiting from the payments. “A retired engineer is receiving their gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving the pension right now. A retired teacher is receiving the pension right now,” he added. The post Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina : La Faso FDA suspend la fabrication et la vente des produits de la gamme « Cyclone » pour présence de sildenafil
items.description: La Faso food and drug administration (Faso FDA) alerte sur la présence de sildénafil dans plusieurs produits de la gamme « Cyclone », commercialisés comme des boissons ou des compléments alimentaires naturels. À titre conservatoire, l'institution a décidé de suspendre leur fabrication et leur vente sur l'ensemble du territoire. Le sildénafil est une substance médicamenteuse utilisée dans le traitement des troubles de l'érection. Son utilisation nécessite toutefois un encadrement médical en raison des risques qu'elle peut présenter pour la santé. Selon la Faso FDA, ces risques concernent particulièrement les personnes souffrant de maladies cardiovasculaires ou d'hypertension, les personnes âgées ainsi que celles qui prennent des dérivés nitrés. La présence de cette substance dans les produits concernés est d'autant plus préoccupante qu'elle ne figure pas sur leur étiquetage. Ces produits sont pourtant présentés aux consommateurs comme des boissons ou des compléments alimentaires « 100 % naturels ». Les produits visés par cette alerte sont au nombre de quatre : cyclone classique, cyclone retard, cyclone sirop et cyclone poudre. La mesure concerne tous les lots, indépendamment de leur date de fabrication ou de leur lieu d'achat. Face à cette situation, la Faso FDA appelle les populations à cesser immédiatement toute consommation de ces produits et à ne plus les acheter. L'institution invite également les personnes qui en ont consommé et qui présentent certains symptômes à se rendre sans délai dans un centre de santé. Il s'agit notamment des douleurs thoraciques, des malaises, des vertiges importants, d'une baisse brutale de la vue ou de l'audition, ainsi que d'une érection douloureuse durant plus de quatre heures. Les personnes concernées sont également invitées à signaler le produit consommé aux professionnels de santé. La mesure de suspension concerne également les acteurs de la chaîne de commercialisation. Grossistes, boutiques, kiosques et vendeurs en ligne sont tenus de retirer immédiatement les produits de la gamme « Cyclone » de leurs stocks et points de vente. La Faso FDA leur demande de les mettre en quarantaine et de se conformer aux instructions des équipes d'inspection chargées de procéder à leur récupération. L'institution invite par ailleurs les consommateurs à faire preuve de vigilance face aux produits qui promettent des effets sur la vigueur sexuelle, la minceur ou encore la guérison de certaines maladies. items.title: Seven companies shortlisted for Keta Port development – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama has announced that seven companies have been shortlisted for the development of the Keta Port in the Volta Region. The companies were selected from 47 that submitted expressions of interest to partner with the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) as strategic partners for the project. Addressing the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival, President Mahama said the shortlisted companies have successfully completed the due diligence stage and will now proceed to the next phase of the process. He explained that the next stage would involve completing the designs and securing financing to pave the way for construction to begin. “Due diligence has been conducted, and the list has been shortlisted to seven companies. These seven companies are proceeding to the next stage, which involves completing the designs and arranging the financing for the project to commence,” he said. The President also disclosed that the administration block for the port, which was started under the previous administration, is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027. “Government remains committed to advancing the project on a credible foundation,” he assured. On other development projects in the Volta Region, President Mahama announced that the Sogakope-Agodome-Keta Water Project, which stalled following Ghana’s debt restructuring, is expected to resume. He said the government signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the contractors in October to facilitate their return to site and the completion of the first phase. On road infrastructure, President Mahama said the Ho-Denu Road is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed in 2027. He added that procurement processes are underway for the reconstruction of the road from Central University at Miotso, near Dawhenya, to Aflao. The government is also working to secure a contractor for the Dabala-Savietula-Keta-Denu Highway. President Mahama further disclosed that several roads in the Anlo area, including the Abor-Atiavi road, has been captured under the World Bank Feeder Roads Project, with procurement expected to begin soon. On healthcare, he said discussions have been initiated during his recent visit to Korea for the resumption of financing for the upgrade of the Volta Regional Hospital in Ho. He said the upgrade would ensure that the facility is befitting of a teaching hospital. The President also announced progress towards establishing a School of Pharmacy under the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS), saying land had been secured and inspected by the committee overseeing its establishment. He said the next steps would involve designing the campus and proceeding to procurement. President Mahama also pledged to support other educational infrastructure requests in the region, including a new dormitory block for Anlo-Afiadenyigba Senior High School, proposed E-Blocks for Shime and Anlo Senior High Schools, and infrastructure improvements at Atiavi Senior High School and Technical School. He further acknowledged calls for the upgrading of Ohawu Agricultural College into a university. On housing, the President said an additional GH¢500 million has been allocated for district housing projects and assured the people of Anlo that the area would benefit. He also said the Anloga 24-hour market project is on track, while preparations for the proposed Aflao Ashigame market have advanced, with land secured and designs completed. According to him, a technical team from China, financed through a grant from the Chinese Government, is expected to visit the project sites to confirm the designs before the release of a US$30 million grant to commence the project. President Mahama urged the Volta Regional Coordinating Council to closely monitor the implementation of the various projects to ensure their timely delivery.

items.title: Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II outdoored as Dorimon chief after four-year dispute
items.description: Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II has been outdoored as the new chief of Dorimon in the Wa West District of the Upper West Region. He was first enskinned on June 3, 2022, but was not outdoored following a protracted dispute, which was later settled in his favour by the Upper West Regional House of Chiefs and the National House of Chiefs. Thursday’s colourful ceremony was unique and grand, with the new chief being outdoored in accordance with the customs and traditional rites of the area. These included jumping over a cow in the presence of chiefs, Imams, queen mothers, security personnel and residents. The Imams, who served as his spiritual godfathers, accompanied him as he walked around the cow while reciting verses from the Holy Quran before he leaped over it. The ceremony was followed by a durbar attended by delegations from Dagbon, Mamprugu, Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire. In his acceptance speech, Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II thanked the people of Dorimon for the honour and appealed to the government to address the numerous challenges facing the area. He said children and generations yet unborn wanted a community united around a common vision. The Member of Parliament for Wa West, retired Superintendent Peter Lanchene Toobu, spoke about roads, culture and peace. He said the roads linking Wa to Dorimon, Dorimon to Wechiau, and Wechiau to Ga had received the attention of the President. Mr Toobu said that during the President’s visit to Wa West, he instructed the Minister for Roads and Highways to ensure that the road was constructed. “Three days ago, I met the Minister for Roads and Highways in Parliament and I asked him what is happening to our road and he said go and tell your chiefs that His Excellency has instructed me to make sure that road is done and I’m making sure that that road is constructed,” he said. He said development was coming and that all that was needed was cooperation and collaboration. A message from the Speaker of Parliament was read by his Principal Marshal, Wing Commander Frederick Bawa. The Speaker urged the new chief to create space for dissent and embrace all those whose perspectives might differ from his. A 60-member delegation from Dagbon, led by the Dalunlanaa, Tafah Mahamudu III, attended the ceremony on behalf of the Kampakuya-Naa, Yakubu Abukari II. The Dalunlanaa said the people of Dagbon stood side by side with Naa Seidu Tungbani Salinbille II. A statement from the Mamprugu Kingdom said the new chief was one of their own, sharing a common lineage, tradition, culture and destiny. It said his forefathers migrated from Mamprugu, settled for some time in Dagbon and eventually moved to Dorimon. Delegations from Gbonaa and Goua in Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire also attended the ceremony. The leader of the delegation from Burkina Faso, Chief Canton de Gaoua, Albert Bifaate II, urged the Presidents of Ghana and Burkina Faso to construct a bridge over the Black Volta. He said the bridge would ensure the easy movement of goods and services and boost trade and commerce between the two countries.

items.title: Lawra Municipal Assembly outlines 2027 development priorities, commits to education and security
items.description: The Lawra Municipal Assembly has held its third ordinary meeting, bringing together key stakeholders to assess the municipality’s progress and outline its development priorities for 2027. Led by the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Cecilia Soyele Nuratu, and the Member of Parliament (MP) for Lawra, Bede Anwataazumo Ziedeng, the meeting highlighted a shared commitment to increased investment in education, improved security and agricultural interventions. Education remains a core priority Education featured prominently as the two municipal leaders outlined extensive support for students in the area. Mr Ziedeng said his office had disbursed more than GH¢785,000 in partial scholarships to support over 660 tertiary students since he began his first term. He added that the individual tertiary scholarship grants had been increased from GH¢1,000 to GH¢2,000 between January 2025 and October 2026, benefiting more than 165 students. At the basic and secondary levels, the MP said he funded mock examinations for Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) candidates at a cost of GH¢84,000 in 2026. He also spent GH¢11,172 on feeding students of Brifoh Senior High School during their examinations. Complementing these efforts, the MCE announced that the Assembly had procured and was distributing essential school furniture. The items include 260 mono desks, 250 dual desks and 100 tables with chairs, aimed at improving the teaching and learning environment across the municipality. Financial commitments and infrastructure updates On the financial well-being of the Assembly’s workforce, Madam Nuratu confirmed receipt of GH¢294,840, which has been earmarked to clear outstanding arrears and cover two quarters’ allowances for Assembly members. The Assembly also presented its 2027 composite budget, fee-fixing resolution and annual action plan for consideration to guide development in the municipality. On infrastructure, the MCE provided an update on the 24-hour economy market project. While acknowledging delays by the contractor, she said the Ministry of Local Government was reviewing the contract to ensure the project’s successful completion. Agricultural interventions and social protection Agriculture, a major contributor to Lawra’s local economy, recorded encouraging results despite some weather-related setbacks. Farmers reported positive harvests, although late rains affected some crops, particularly groundnuts. To support local livelihoods, the government introduced interventions, including the distribution of free fertiliser, drip irrigation equipment and 10,000 chicks to farmers. However, the MCE expressed concern about the high mortality rate among the poultry distributed to beneficiaries. In the area of social protection, the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme continues to extend support to vulnerable residents. The Assembly is processing payments and onboarding approximately 4,700 beneficiaries in the municipality. Health and security surveillance Although Lawra remains generally peaceful, the MCE raised concerns about recent security incidents, particularly two robbery cases reported along the Nandom road. She said the police had arrested two suspects and recovered a weapon, while efforts were ongoing to track down the main suspect, who remains at large. Security agencies are expected to intensify day and night patrols to maintain law and order during the upcoming festive season and the funeral rites of the late Paramount Chief of Lawra. Health officials have also stepped up surveillance following reports of yellow fever outbreaks in neighbouring districts. The management of the municipal hospital has urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report symptoms of acute fever or jaundice to the nearest health facility to help prevent an outbreak in the municipality. As Assembly members deliberated on the 2027 budget, the meeting highlighted the need for continued collaboration among local government officials and stakeholders to address infrastructure challenges, improve education and healthcare, support livelihoods and strengthen security across the municipality.

items.title: Développement local participatif : Le maire de commune Golfe 6, Kokou Amenyenou échange avec les artisans
items.description: Lomé, 7 nov. (ATOP) – Le maire de la commune Golfe 6, Kokou Amenyenou a échangé, le vendredi 6 novembre à Baguida, chef-lieu de la commune, avec les artisans sur leur rôle et responsabilité dans le développement du milieu. La rencontre a réuni les responsables des différentes organisations des artisans, notamment des couturières et couturiers, des maçons et plombiers, des mécaniciens et vulgarisateurs. Les échanges ont permis à ces artisans de mieux cerner l’importance de leur secteur dans le développement de la commune et leur contribution dans la réalisation du budget. Le maire Amenyenou a appelé les artisans de sa commune au civisme fiscal, en leur faisant savoir que dans la dynamique de la mobilisation des recettes, leur apport et contribution s’avèrent importante. Il a exhorté ceux qui ont accumulé des arriérés de paiement de taxes, de vite régulariser leur situation. Le maire a informé que dans le budget prochain, certaines taxes ont été revues à la baisse, notamment celles liées à la libération des apprentis, pour permettre une facilité de collecte. Les artisans ont, à travers leur porte-parole, Logossou Yao Ben, félicité le maire pour cette démarche. Ils se sont engagés pour un développement local et formulé des doléances en vue d’une bonne collaboration. Leurs préoccupations sont relatives, entre autres, à la taxe forfaitaire unique à payer par tous les artisans, à la simplification des modalités de payement, à la dotation des artisans d’une chambre de métiers ou un centre communautaire pour l’organisation de leurs activités collectives. Des questions liées aux plaques publicitaires des ateliers, au renforcement des capacités des artisans, au programme social pour les enfants vulnérables, à l’insécurité dans certaines zones de la commune, ont été aussi évoquées. Les responsables syndicaux ont aussi soulevé les difficultés de mobilisations de tous les artisans dans leur corporation en vue de répondre aux sollicitations de la mairie. Au regard de ces doléances, le maire a promis prendre des dispositions pour satisfaire leurs préoccupations, et rendre la collaboration simple entre les artisans et la municipalité. Il a également évoqué la prochaine visite d’un conseil municipal du Sénégal à Baguida pour un partage d’expériences. M. Amenyenou a saisi cette occasion pour demander aux artisans de sensibiliser leurs pairs sur la libération des emprises des voies bitumées et pavées de la ville, entamée dans le District autonome du Grand Lomé. ATOP/KYA/DHK

items.title: Nepra raises special industrial tariff to Rs25.30 per unit, despite dissent
items.description: • Two members oppose revision, saying actual marginal cost stands at Rs31.83/unit • Power regulator warns of package suspension and legal action over missed deadlines • Consumers to pay an additional Rs2.37/unit in Nov bills to recover Rs25bn under fuel cost adjustment ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday announced a controversial revision of a special electricity tariff introduced as an incentive to revive industrial activity, while approving an additional burden of Rs2.37 per unit on electricity consumers for November. The decision, opposed by the industrial sector, is likely to have a negative impact on all electricity consumers, including those served by K-Electric and other distribution companies (Discos). All four members of the regulator unanimously held the Power Division and its subordinate entities responsible for failing to fulfil their legal obligations within the prescribed timelines, pushing Nepra into an unprecedented deadlock and potentially increasing costs for electricity consumers across the country. At the centre of the controversy was an incremental support package (ISP) of Rs22.98 per unit introduced for industrial consumers in December last year. Industrialists have been protesting against the package since May, seeking its suspension on the grounds that it had failed to benefit them and was instead increasing their electricity bills. The package was due for a review after the completion of its first six months in June, based on the lessons learnt during its implementation. Following a belated request from the Power Division, despite repeated reminders from the regulator, Nepra on Friday revised the ISP rate to Rs25.30 per unit. The decision was strongly opposed by its two most relevant members, those responsible for tariff and development matters. Interestingly, Nepra Chairman Waseem Mukhtar fully endorsed the written arguments and positions taken by the dissenting members but subsequently exercised his special casting vote to approve the revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit instead of retaining the existing rate of Rs22.98. The authority was divided 2-2 on the matter. Member Tariff Amina Ahmed and Member Development Maqsood Anwar, in a joint dissenting note, maintained that even the proposed revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit was a “random number” unsupported by evidence. They said Nepra’s own institutional calculations put the marginal cost at Rs31.83 per unit rather than Rs25.30. “The revised incremental rate of Rs25.30 per unit proposed by the Ministry of Energy (MoE), and allowed by the honourable Chairman and Member (Law), is based on the generation mix apparently assumed at the design stage of the package, with updated fuel prices,” the two members observed. They called for the immediate suspension of the ISP until authentic data became available. The dissenting members argued that compliance with the federal cabinet’s decision and Nepra’s own directives required a reassessment of the existing rate of Rs22.98 per unit to determine whether it should be retained, revised or suspended. However, this exercise had not been carried out, resulting in the continuation of the package at a rate below the actual cost of supplying incremental electricity. “The resulting misalignment has had implications for consumers in two ways. First, to the extent incremental consumption increased the system’s average fuel cost, the resulting impact was recovered from all consumers through the FCA mechanism. Second, because incremental units are excluded from quarterly tariff adjustments, the exclusion of such units increases the quarterly adjustment borne by consumers not availing the package,” they said. The two members, therefore, recommended the temporary suspension of the tariff package rather than choosing the proposed rate of Rs25.30 or above per unit. They questioned how a package based on the principle of cost-reflectivity could continue without a validated cost-reflective rate. They argued that since the alternative rate had no credible link with the actual marginal cost, continuation of the package was no longer justified. They said other consumers should not be made to bear the cost of a review that the MoE was required to submit five months ago but had yet to provide. In his casting vote, Nepra Chairman Waseem Mukhtar observed that the dissenting members’ conclusions “need serious consideration”. However, he said suspending the package at this stage would not be appropriate and that the Ministry of Energy should be given another opportunity to provide the information repeatedly sought by the regulator, including in its latest determination. All four members agreed that the Power Division was required to submit revised calculations six months ago but had failed to do so despite repeated reminders from Nepra. They also regretted that the ministry had not responded adequately to the questions and queries raised by the regulator. “The marginal price, in proper form, was not provided to the regulator by either the Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO) or the Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC), which were duty-bound to do so. Since the ISP is a flagship project of the ministry, it should give due consideration to the observations of Nepra and the lack of inter-agency coordination among the entities working under the ministry,” the members observed. The determination also sets deadlines for the relevant entities to provide the required information. The four members warned that failure to meet these deadlines could lead to an adverse outcome in the review of the programme, including its suspension or termination. “Furthermore, any entity that fails to provide the required information within the stipulated timeline shall lead to initiation of legal proceedings under the applicable legal framework,” they stated. Explaining his decision, Nepra chairman said: “I hereby exercise, in due and faithful discharge of the functions of the Authority, my second and casting vote envisaged and entrusted to me under the Nepra Act in favour of the First Opinion, thereby breaking the deadlock in relation to the aforesaid issues. Accordingly, the First Opinion constitutes the Order of the Authority.” Meanwhile, Nepra allowed power distribution companies to charge an additional Rs2.37 per unit from all consumers in their November bills under the monthly fuel cost adjustment (FCA) mechanism to recover an additional Rs25 billion. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: WPL 2026/27: Hasaacas Ladies come from behind to beat Epiphany Warriors
items.description: Hasaacas Ladies continued their impressive start to the 2026/27 GoldFields Women’s Premier League following their victory over Epiphany Warriors. Hasaacas came from a goal down to claim all three points at the Madina Astro Turf, securing a 2-1 victory over the Katamanso-based side. Epiphany came into the fixture looking for their first win of the season after picking up two draws in their opening two games in league. Hasaacas, on the other hand, are breaming with confidence following back-to-back wins over Army Ladies and Jonina Ladies in the first two games of the campaign. Making her first appearance following her involvement in the 2026 U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, Jessica Appiah Asamoah opened the scoring for Epiphany after just two minutes. The winger burst forward on the right flank, setting up a one-on-one situation with Grace Banwaa before putting the ball past the goalkeeper. Epiphany took control of the game and continued possession but failed to add to their lead. Seventeen minutes after taking the lead, the home side conceded a penalty which was converted by Belinda Kpoglo to draw the Hasmal Ladies level. Hasaacas grew into the game and for a brief moment had the upper hand over Epiphany and was rewarded for it when Comfort Owusu was fouled in the opposition’s box. Kpoglo stepped up once again to hand the Takoradi-based side the lead in the 31st minute. Despite their spirited attempts, Epiphany were unable to get back on level terms and were handed their first defeat of the season. The victory means Hasaacas have won all of their three games this season, staying on level terms with Police Ladies, who also came from a goal down to beat newly promoted Roots Sistaz.

items.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
items.description: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also hit with bans and fines, as was Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina’s coaching team. In a statement, AFA said FIFA’s appeals body had rejected their complaint against the sanctions handed out to Paredes and the association, but had reduced Molina’s punishment from a seven-match ban and $90,000 fine to four games and $60,000. AFA also stated it would now take its appeals against its own and Paredes’s sanctions to CAS. The post Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: France : des milliers de personnes dans la rue pour "maintenir la pression"
items.description: Pour le quatrième samedi consécutif, des milliers de personnes descendent dans la rue en France pour essayer de « maintenir la pression » avant une rencontre lundi avec le gouvernement et deux jours après une mobilisation d'ampleur. « Je suis ici pour dénoncer les violences policières et le manque de réponses à nos revendications », a déclaré à l'AFP Emna, lycéenne de 16 ans, rencontrée à Paris sur la place de la République, d'où s'est élancée dans le calme la marche dans la capitale. Le cortège parisien est majoritairement composé de jeunes, lycéens, étudiants, trentenaires, qui défilent notamment au son du tube de Téléphone « Je rêvais d'un autre monde ». À 14h, la mobilisation était toutefois en net recul sur l'ensemble du territoire, selon l'entourage du ministre de l'Intérieur, qui a évoqué une situation « globalement calme et maîtrisée » , avec 18 interpellations, contre 27 à la même heure la semaine précédente. De son côté, l'intersyndicale de la jeunesse a fait état de 250.000 manifestants en France, dont 75.000 à Paris. « Ce n'est pas parce que les négociations doivent débuter » lundi à Matignon autour du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu « que la mobilisation doit se terminer », a jugé Vincent Gautheron, secrétaire général de l'Union régionale CGT, au départ de la manifestation parisienne organisée par l'intersyndicale de jeunesse (Union étudiante, Fage, Unef et USL) et des unions syndicales régionales (CGT, FO, FSU, Solidaires, CFDT). « Aujourd'hui, c'est une date qui permet de maintenir la pression », a déclaré pour sa part Sabrine Kharbach, porte-parole de l'Union étudiante. Du côté de la place de la Concorde, dans le centre de la capitale, les forces de l'ordre étaient venues en nombre pour empêcher un autre rassemblement, prévu par la coordination des gilets jaunes et interdit par la préfecture de police. En début d'après-midi, très peu de manifestants tentaient de s'y rassembler et deux porte-paroles de la coordination, Benjamin Ball et Azelma Sigaux, ont été interpellés par la police, a constaté l'AFP. Un rassemblement prévu plus tôt dans la matinée par des gilets jaunes près de la Tour Eiffel n'a finalement pas eu lieu. À Clermont-Ferrand, environ 600 personnes se sont rassemblées selon la préfecture, dans une ambiance bon enfant et à l'écart du centre-ville, où tout rassemblement était interdit. À Lyon, les forces de l’ordre ont tiré des gaz lacrymogènes pour disperser « plusieurs centaines de personnes occupant la voie publique dans le cadre d’un rassemblement non déclaré », situé dans un périmètre du centre-ville interdit de rassemblement, a indiqué la préfecture. Maintenir la pression La nouvelle journée de mobilisation vise à garder de l'élan deux jours avant une conférence sociale avec les syndicats et le patronat, convoquée lundi matin à Matignon, et des rencontres avec les organisations lycéennes et étudiantes l’après-midi. Cette conférence « permettra de présenter les réponses concrètes aux attentes des Français » , a assuré le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, dans un courrier adressé vendredi aux partenaires sociaux. Les autorités veulent à tout prix éviter que se reproduisent les scènes d'émeutes et de pillages du 17 octobre. Le dispositif massif de sécurité en vigueur depuis lors a été « reconduit » , avec 70.000 policiers et gendarmes mobilisés sur l'ensemble du territoire, a annoncé vendredi le ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez. « Le risque est exactement le même que pour les samedis précédents » , a-t-il souligné, appelant les préfets à « ne pas baisser la garde face à des phénomènes plus éclatés voire sporadiques dont le niveau de violence ne baissera pas en intensité ». Samedi à Paris, place de la République, la plupart des magasins étaient ouverts, avec des vitrines protégées par des planches de bois, mais, sur le parcours de la manifestation, la majorité des boutiques étaient fermées. Ne pas attendre la présidentielle La suite du mouvement dépendra en grande partie des réponses que va apporter le gouvernement lundi lors de la conférence sociale. Les huit principaux syndicats nationaux ont d'ores et déjà indiqué qu'ils prendraient position dès lundi soir. Une intersyndicale de l'éducation, rassemblant syndicats lycéens (USL), étudiants (Union étudiante, Unef, Fage, Fédération nationale étudiante) ainsi qu'enseignants et personnels (FSU, FO, CGT, SUD), a d'ores et déjà appelé à une journée de grève et manifestation mardi. The post France : des milliers de personnes dans la rue pour "maintenir la pression" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : La lutte sénégalaise frappe fort avec deux finales et deux médailles assurées
items.description: Le Sénégal tient une belle promesse de médailles aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. La lutte, sport profondément ancré dans l'identité et les traditions du pays, porte haut les couleurs nationales avec deux athlètes qualifiés en finale. La lutte sénégalaise répond présent au rendez-vous de Dakar 2026. Alors que les compétitions se poursuivent, les représentants du pays hôte affichent une détermination à la hauteur de l'événement. Élisabeth Diatta a ouvert la voie en se qualifiant pour la finale des -50 kg. Dans son sillage, Maguette Diop a réussi à franchir les étapes de sa catégorie des -80 kg pour s'offrir, lui aussi, une place en finale. Deux finales, deux occasions de décrocher l'or et, surtout, deux médailles déjà garanties pour le Sénégal. Avec ces qualifications, le pays est assuré de remporter au minimum deux médailles d'argent en lutte. Un premier bilan particulièrement encourageant pour une discipline qui incarne une part importante du patrimoine sportif et culturel sénégalais. Au-delà de la performance individuelle des deux athlètes, cet exploit revêt une dimension symbolique. Dans un pays où la lutte dépasse largement le cadre du sport pour occuper une place singulière dans la culture populaire, ces résultats donnent un relief particulier à la participation sénégalaise aux JOJ. La discipline, véritable sport bien de chez nous, démontre qu'elle peut aussi rayonner sur la scène olympique et contribuer au rayonnement international du Sénégal. Ces deux finales constituent également un motif de satisfaction pour le pays organisateur. Après avoir relevé le défi de l'organisation de cette première édition olympique de la jeunesse sur le continent africain, le Sénégal entend aussi réussir celui de la participation. Voir ses jeunes athlètes briller à domicile, dans une discipline aussi emblématique, donne une saveur particulière à cette aventure. Et l'histoire pourrait être encore plus belle. Les deux finalistes auront désormais l'occasion de transformer leurs médailles d'argent assurées en or. Pendant ce temps, les autres combats se poursuivent, avec l'espoir de voir la moisson sénégalaise s'enrichir davantage. À Dakar 2026, la lutte sénégalaise ne se contente pas de défendre les couleurs nationales : elle s'affirme déjà comme l'un des grands atouts du Sénégal dans sa quête de médailles. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Exim Bank to commence a 200-acre textile and garment industrial hub for Weta, targeting 3,000 jobs – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to establish a light industrial area dedicated to textile and garment manufacturing at Weta in the Volta Region through the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank). The President said 200 acres of land had been acquired for the project, which is expected to create thousands of employment opportunities when fully operational. Speaking at the grand durbar of the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival in Anloga, President Mahama said he had commissioned the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank) to commence work on the industrial enclave. He said the project would initially create approximately 3,000 jobs, with the figure expected to increase to 10,000 as operations expand. “We have commissioned the Ghana EXIM Bank to commence work on a Light Industrial Area in the Weta area. Two hundred acres of land have been acquired,” he noted. “This industrial area will be dedicated to the textile and garment industry,” the president added. “We expect that initially, when it starts, it will create some 3,000 jobs and grow eventually to 10,000 jobs when it is fully operational,” Mr Mahama disclosed. The proposed Weta industrial area is expected to strengthen the Volta Region’s industrial base, particularly in textile and garment production, while creating employment opportunities for residents, CEO of the EXIM Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, said in September during the 2026 yam festival of the chiefs and people of Asogli Traditional Area. President Mahama’s announcement follows a similar investment in the Northern Region, where President Mahama in August 2026 commissioned the Northshore Apparel Ghana Limited factory at Savelugu. The facility, funded through a partnership involving Ghana EXIM Bank, Germany’s KfW Development Bank and the Agricultural Development Bank, is designed to manufacture garments for local and international markets. The Northshore Apparel project has already created employment for more than 2,300 people, with the workforce expected to increase to 10,000 when the facility reaches full operational capacity. President Mahama described the Savelugu facility as a major step towards restoring Northern Ghana’s industrial prominence and advancing the government’s 24-hour economy agenda. The proposed Weta project, also expected to be supported by Ghana EXIM Bank, signals the government’s intention to extend garment and textile manufacturing investments to other parts of the country.

items.title: Bono East Regional Minister pledges gov’t support for Kintampo North development at Pedia Festival
items.description: The Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, joined the Member of Parliament for Kintampo North, Joseph Kwame Kumah (Jakala), and the Municipal Chief Executive, Isaac Donkor, to celebrate this year’s Pedia (Yam) Festival with the Mo Paramount Chief, Nana Kwaku Danquah III, and Nananom of the Mo Traditional Council. The event, held under the theme “ Rebuilding Our Cultural Heritage: Preserving Our Roots, Shaping Our Future ,” attracted several dignitaries, including MDCEs from Techiman South, Techiman North, Nkoranza North, and Kintampo South, as well as constituency executives from Kintampo North and South. Addressing the gathering, Mr Owusu Antwi conveyed greetings from President John Dramani Mahama and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to working with traditional authorities to develop Kintampo North. “Government recognizes the critical role of traditional institutions in national development, and we will continue to work closely with Nananom to advance the development aspirations of our communities,” he stated. He commended the festival’s theme, noting that cultural preservation is key to national identity and unity. He also urged the youth to promote peace and tolerance, and called on Nananom to remain united for the community’s progress. “A united traditional authority provides a solid foundation for peace, stability, and sustainable development. I urge our youth to embrace responsible conduct and mutual respect rather than resort to actions that could threaten our peaceful coexistence,” the Minister added. The Minister highlighted key projects for Kintampo North, including road construction, educational and healthcare infrastructure, the 24-Hour Economy Market, and the Farmers Service Centre. In support of the celebration, Comrade Prince Opoku Mensah, Bono East Regional Organizer, presented GH₵50,000 on behalf of the government and party towards Nananom’s fundraising efforts. Nana Kwaku Danquah III thanked the Minister and dignitaries for their participation and reaffirmed the Mo community’s commitment to peace, unity, and development. “The Mo community stands for peace, unity, and development. We are grateful to the government for its continued support and engagement with our traditional council,” the Mo Paramount Chief said.

items.title: Norvège : les six F-16 promis à Kiev au cœur d'une polémique sur les retards et les coûts
items.description: En avril 2026, les six F-16 norvegiens promis a Kiev se trouvaient encore dans des ateliers de maintenance en Belgique. Dans une tribune publiee le 5 novembre sur le site Steigan, Dan-Viggo Bergtun, veteran et ancien responsable d'organisations de veterans, critique ces retards et demande des comptes sur les depenses engagees. Pour les six F-16 destines a Kiev, l'echeance avait ete fixee a 2024. Jonas Gahr Store, Premier ministre norvegien, l'avait annonce le 10 juillet de cette annee-la. Or, le 7 avril 2026, les avions se trouvaient encore en Belgique. La radiotelevision publique norvegienne NRK indiquait qu'ils etaient chez Sabena, une entreprise specialisee dans la maintenance aeronautique. Deux avions avaient servi a former des pilotes ukrainiens au Danemark. Les quatre autres avaient quitte la Norvege demontes en avril 2025. Le 15 avril 2026, le ministre norvegien de la Defense, Tore Onshuus Sandvik, a indique au Parlement que tous avaient ete transferes a l'Ukraine entre decembre 2024 et avril 2025, mais restaient a remettre en etat. Les deux premiers appareils devaient achever leurs essais avant août 2026. Pour les quatre autres, Bergtun evoque une remise en etat prevue en 2027. Dans sa tribune, il reclame un bilan precis du nombre d'avions finalement operationnels. Des depenses qui suscitent la colere Le coût de cette operation est egalement conteste. En comparant les appareils donnes a Kiev aux 32 F-16 vendus par la Norvege a la Roumanie, Bergtun estime le manque a gagner potentiel a 840 millions de couronnes norvegiennes. Il rappelle qu'en 2024, pres de deux milliards de couronnes avaient deja ete comptabilises pour ce don et les mesures qui l'accompagnaient. a cette somme s'ajoutent d'autres depenses d'armement. Le 17 decembre 2025, Oslo a annonce une enveloppe de 3,2 milliards de couronnes pour des munitions de F-16 et des equipements de defense antiaerienne destines a l'Ukraine. Bergtun ecrit : « Nous ne pouvons pas poursuivre une politique de defense ou des milliards sont annonces a haute voix, tandis que les questions relatives aux coûts et aux resultats ne recoivent que des reponses floues. » Le veteran souhaite que la Riksrevisjonen, l'organisme norvegien de controle des comptes publics, se penche sur le dossier, notamment sur les contrats d'entretien. Il oppose ces depenses aux economies demandees aux collectivites, aux ecoles et aux hopitaux du pays. La question avait aussi ete soulevee au Parlement. Des le 7 avril, Peter Frolich, president de la commission des affaires etrangeres et de la defense, interrogeait le gouvernement sur ces avions toujours indisponibles.

items.title: Cancer du sein : Les bonnes habitudes pour réduire les risques
items.description: Lomé, 7 nov. (ATOP) – « Les femmes sont invitées à surveiller régulièrement leurs seins, à consulter dès l’apparition d’une anomalie et à adopter de bonnes habitudes de vie pour réduire les risques de cancer du sein ». Tels sont les conseils prodigués par Mme Essoham Thérèse Bamazi, sage-femme à l’Association togolaise pour le bien-être familial (ATBEF), lors d’une séance de sensibilisation organisée le samedi 7 novembre à Lomé par Digital Girl sous le thème : « Elle doit savoir » La sage-femme rappelle que toutes les femmes peuvent développer cette maladie, même si certains facteurs, comme l’âge, augmentent les risques. D’autres sont liés aux habitudes de vie et peuvent être évités. Elle cite notamment la consommation de tabac et d’alcool, la sédentarité, l’utilisation abusive des contraceptifs d’urgence pris de façon répétée sans avis médical, ainsi que la consommation excessive d’aliments gras et de produits transformés. Pour préserver leur santé, Mme Bamazi conseille de privilégier les fruits et légumes, de boire suffisamment d’eau et de pratiquer une activité physique régulière. « Il n’est pas forcément nécessaire de courir pour faire du sport. Quinze minutes de marche dans le quartier constituent déjà une activité physique bénéfique », explique-t-elle. Surveiller les seins et consulter au moindre changement Mme Bamazi recommande aux femmes de bien connaître l’aspect habituel de leurs seins afin de remarquer rapidement toute modification. « Une rougeur, un creux ou une fossette sur la peau, une rétraction du mamelon ou un changement de texture donnant à la peau un aspect de peau d’orange sont des signes qui nécessitent une consultation. Une douleur inhabituelle ou un écoulement au niveau du mamelon doit également retenir l’attention », indique-t-elle. « Même si l’on pense que ce n’est rien, il vaut mieux aller à l’hôpital pour se faire examiner plutôt que de rester à la maison », conseille-t-elle. Elle encourage également les femmes à consulter régulièrement un agent de santé pour un examen clinique des seins. « En cas de suspicion d’une anomalie, une échographie mammaire ou une mammographie peut être prescrite. Une biopsie peut ensuite être réalisée, si nécessaire, pour confirmer ou écarter le diagnostic de cancer. Le cancer du sein ne prévient pas, mais l’information, la vigilance et le dépistage peuvent changer le cours d’une vie », mentionne-t-elle. ATOP/AO/AR

items.title: Re-election: Tinubu lists economy, education, healthcare as priorities
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has pledged to give priority attention to education, economic recovery, healthcare and citizens’ welfare if given another mandate in 2027. Tinubu made the pledge at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt on Saturday. Speaking at the rally co-organised by the Rainbow Coalition led by Chief Nyesom Wike, the Minister, Federal Capital Territory, Tinubu also said that youth development would be given deserved attention. The president urged Rivers people to use their Permanent Voter Cards wisely to achieve a better and more progressive Nigeria. He expressed his administration’s commitment to promote the welfare of retirees through enhanced and prompt payment of pensions and gratuities. He commended Wike and the people of Rivers for massively expressing their resolve to support his re-election bid. The president thanked Wike for his commitment to reconciliation and peace-building during the political crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu also commended Gov. Siminalayi Fubara for being a peaceful leader and lover of his state, saying, “The governor will never regret his commitment to restoring peace in the state.” “I sincerely appreciate Wike, Fubara, APC members and the Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council for their support,” he said. Earlier, Wike assured the president that Rivers residents would massively support his re-election bid. He said that Tinubu had demonstrated huge support to the state by appointing no fewer than 47 Rivers people into strategic positions at the national level. “We cannot take the president’s support for granted. Rivers people will vote massively for the president in the 2027 presidential election,” he said. Also speaking, Fubara said that Rivers would deliver no fewer than three million votes in support of the president’s re-election bid. “We shall continue to work together to ensure that the president wins the election; that is our promise,” he said. He thanked the campaign team for providing an opportunity for Rivers people to demonstrate their political strength and support for the president. Fubara thanked Tinubu for his commitment to the development of the Niger Delta Region through critical infrastructure projects, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that while in the state, Tinubu inaugurated the Bonny-Bodo Road project. He also presented the APC governorship flag to the party’s candidate in Rivers, Mr Kingsley Chinda. (NAN) The post Re-election: Tinubu lists economy, education, healthcare as priorities appeared first on Vanguard News .
