items.title: Carburants : le PJD questionne la concurrence, la hausse des prix et le blocage de La Samir
items.description: La persistance de prix élevés des carburants au Maroc, y compris lorsque les cours internationaux du pétrole enregistrent des baisses, suscite de nouvelles critiques au sein du Parti de la justice et du développement (PJD). Le groupe parlementaire du parti à la Chambre des représentants dénonce un marché caractérisé par un manque de transparence et une concurrence insuffisante, appelant à mettre fin aux pratiques abusives de certaines entreprises du secteur. Dans des déclarations à la presse, Abdellah Hamel, député du PJD, a souligné les difficultés rencontrées par les consommateurs face à la hausse des prix des carburants. « Les Marocains ont subi de plein fouet la flambée excessive des prix des carburants », a-t-il affirmé, pointant notamment l’incompréhension suscitée par la poursuite de cette tendance sur le marché national. L’élu s’est particulièrement interrogé sur le décalage entre l’évolution des cours du pétrole à l’international et les prix pratiqués au Maroc. Il estime difficile pour les citoyens de comprendre pourquoi les tarifs continuent d’augmenter dans le Royaume, même durant les périodes où les marchés internationaux enregistrent une baisse des prix du pétrole. Au-delà de la question des tarifs, le parlementaire a dénoncé l’absence de véritable concurrence sur le marché des carburants. Il s’est interrogé sur les raisons de la persistance de cette situation, estimant que le manque de transparence dans le secteur appelle des réponses de la part des pouvoirs publics. Hamel a également questionné le gouvernement sur le respect de ses engagements antérieurs concernant le renforcement de la transparence et la surveillance des entreprises opérant dans le secteur des carburants. Il a rappelé que le PJD avait déjà demandé à la ministre chargée du secteur de tenir sa promesse de mettre fin au manque de transparence au sein des sociétés pétrolières. Pour le groupe parlementaire, la persistance de la cherté des carburants soulève des interrogations sur les mécanismes de fixation des prix au Maroc. La question porte également sur la manière dont les fluctuations des marchés internationaux sont répercutées sur les tarifs appliqués aux consommateurs marocains, dans un contexte où le manque de concurrence demeure au cœur des critiques. La raffinerie Samir au cœur des interrogations Le député a par ailleurs remis sur la table la question de la raffinerie La Samir , dont l’arrêt prolongé continue de susciter des interrogations. Il s’est demandé quelles étaient les raisons de la persistance de cette situation et quelles parties étaient responsables du blocage de sa remise en service. Les interrogations portent notamment sur la possibilité de reprendre les activités de raffinage, alors que la relance de cette installation est présentée comme un enjeu important dans le débat sur la sécurité énergétique nationale. Abdellah Hamel a ainsi souligné que le dossier de la remise en activité de La Samir devait être abordé dans le cadre d’une réflexion plus large sur le renforcement de la sécurité énergétique du Maroc. L’objectif, selon lui, est de permettre au pays et à ses citoyens de tirer profit de la relance de la raffinerie. The post Carburants : le PJD questionne la concurrence, la hausse des prix et le blocage de La Samir appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Des sièges à l’influence : inscrire dans la durée les avancées politiques des femmes à São Tomé-et-Príncipe (Par Yoshio Ando et Luc Gnonlonfoun)
items.description: À l’issue des élections législatives de 2026, l’Assemblée nationale de São Tomé-et-Príncipe comptera 19 femmes parmi ses 55 membres, contre huit dans la législature précédente. La proportion de sièges occupés par des femmes passe ainsi de 14,5 % à 34,5 %. Derrière ces chiffres se trouve une avancée majeure pour la représentation politique et pour la démocratie santoméenne. Une avancée qu’il faut saluer, mais surtout consolider . Ce résultat n’est ni un hasard ni l’œuvre d’un acteur isolé. Il traduit d’abord une décision souveraine du pays : l’adoption, en 2022, d’une loi sur la parité qui prévoit une représentation minimale de 40 % de chaque sexe sur les listes de candidatures et fixe des règles de positionnement. Les élections de 2026 ont constitué la première mise à l’épreuve de ce nouveau cadre lors d’un scrutin législatif. Elles montrent qu’une réforme juridique peut produire des changements concrets lorsqu’elle s’accompagne d’une volonté politique, d’un suivi rigoureux et d’une mobilisation collective. Les institutions nationales ont joué un rôle déterminant dans cette évolution. La « Comissão de Seguimento da Lei da Paridade » a notamment examiné les listes de candidatures et encouragé les ajustements nécessaires avant leur validation. Les autorités électorales et juridictionnelles, les partis politiques, les organisations de la société civile et les femmes engagées dans la vie publique ont, chacun dans leur rôle, contribué à faire vivre la loi. L’expérience rappelle également qu’une première application, même porteuse de progrès, doit être évaluée avec lucidité : des difficultés de conformité et de mise en œuvre demeurent et constituent autant d’enseignements pour les prochaines échéances. Les femmes elles-mêmes ont été au cœur de cette dynamique. Au cours du processus électoral, 72 femmes issues de sept partis politiques et de cinq districts ont bénéficié de formations portant notamment sur la communication politique, la négociation et la prévention des violences à l’égard des femmes en politique. Un réseau de plus de 105 personnes, rassemblant des parlementaires, des acteurs des partis et des journalistes, a porté le plaidoyer public en faveur de la parité. Des échanges avec des parlementaires du Cap Vert ont également ouvert des perspectives de partage d’expérience et de mentorat. Ces résultats sont avant tout ceux de São Tomé-et-Príncipe. Ils illustrent aussi ce que peut apporter une coopération internationale fondée sur les priorités nationales, l’écoute et la complémentarité des compétences. Avec le soutien financier du Gouvernement du Japon et de ressources internes, le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) a accompagné les institutions et les parties prenantes nationales au cours du cycle électoral de 2026, notamment dans l’application du nouveau cadre juridique, le dialogue, la sensibilisation et le renforcement des capacités. Pour le Japon, cet engagement s’inscrit dans les principes défendus depuis 1993 dans le cadre de la Conférence internationale de Tokyo sur le développement de l’Afrique (TICAD) : l’appropriation africaine du développement durable, de la paix et de la stabilité, fondée sur la bonne gouvernance, la démocratie et l’état de droit. Cet engagement japonais, en faveur de la confiance et de l’inclusion, prend une résonance particulière en cette année du 50e anniversaire des relations diplomatiques entre le Japon et São Tomé-et-Príncipe. Pour le PNUD, il confirme la valeur d’un accompagnement de long terme des institutions et de la gouvernance inclusive. La mobilisation du Coordonnateur résident des Nations Unies, d’ONU Femmes et d’autres partenaires du système des Nations Unies a renforcé la complémentarité de cette action, dans le respect du leadership national. Une nouvelle étape commence désormais. Sur les 19 élues, 16 n’avaient pas encore exercé de mandat électif. Comme tout parlementaire entrant en fonction pour la première fois, elles auront à s’approprier les procédures de l’Assemblée, le travail en commission, l’examen des textes, le contrôle de l’action publique et le débat budgétaire. Elles devront pouvoir le faire dans un environnement propice à une participation pleine et entière, à l’abri des intimidations et des violences, y compris dans l’espace numérique. Passer des sièges à l’influence ne signifie donc pas seulement accroître la visibilité des élues. Cela signifie créer les conditions pour qu’elles puissent exercer effectivement leur mandat, contribuer aux priorités nationales et prendre part aux responsabilités parlementaires, dans le respect des règles de l’institution et des prérogatives de ses membres. Les institutions parlementaires et les acteurs politiques ont, chacun à leur niveau, un rôle à jouer pour favoriser des pratiques inclusives, un dialogue de qualité et une participation équitable des femmes et des hommes aux décisions. Cette ambition peut également s’appuyer sur la solidarité et le dialogue entre parlementaires, au-delà des sensibilités politiques. Le Réseau des femmes parlementaires peut constituer un espace utile de partage d’expérience, de formation et d’échanges sur les questions d’intérêt général. L’accompagnement des nouvelles élues gagnera à associer expertise parlementaire, mentorat, communication publique et mécanismes de prévention des violences politiques. Il doit rester non partisan et respecter pleinement l’indépendance de l’Assemblée nationale. L’enjeu dépasse cette seule législature. Il est aussi de préserver les acquis de la loi, de tirer les enseignements de son application, de renforcer la confiance des citoyens dans les institutions démocratiques et d’ouvrir des perspectives à la prochaine génération de femmes leaders. Dans ce processus, les organisations de femmes, les jeunes, les médias et la société civile ont un rôle essentiel à jouer. La participation politique doit devenir une possibilité réelle, dans toutes les régions du pays, et non une exception réservée à quelques parcours. Le Japon et le PNUD restent attachés à cette ambition commune. En dialogue avec les autorités nationales et les partenaires concernés, le PNUD examine les modalités d’un accompagnement au Parlement de manière générale et des femmes parlementaires plus particulièrement pour consolider les compétences, la participation et le leadership. Le Japon continuera de valoriser les enseignements de cette coopération et de poursuivre le dialogue avec ses partenaires sur les moyens de soutenir des institutions démocratiques inclusives. Les prochaines étapes devront être définies avec les acteurs nationaux, en fonction de leurs priorités et des ressources mobilisables. Les élections de 2026 ont ouvert un chapitre nouveau. Le défi est maintenant collectif : veiller à ce que la représentation accrue des femmes se traduise par une participation effective aux décisions, des institutions plus ouvertes et des possibilités élargies pour les générations futures. La portée de cette avancée ne se mesurera pas seulement au nombre de sièges conquis, mais à la capacité de toutes les élues et de tous les élus à servir ensemble l’intérêt général. C’est ainsi que les progrès d’aujourd’hui pourront devenir les acquis durables de demain. Yoshio Ando est Ambassadeur du Japon près São Tomé-et-Príncipe. Luc Gnonlonfoun est Représentant résident du Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) à São Tomé-et-Príncipe.

items.title: OM : Bruno Genesio salue le retour en force de Nayef Aguerd
items.description: Le retour au premier plan de Nayef Aguerd ne laisse pas son entraîneur indifférent. En conférence de presse, Bruno Genesio est revenu en détail sur la montée en puissance du défenseur central international marocain sous le maillot de l'Olympique de Marseille, soulignant la force mentale dont l'intéressé a dû faire preuve pour surmonter une période particulièrement délicate de sa carrière. Revenant sur les épreuves traversées par le défenseur des Lions de l'Atlas, le technicien a rappelé la complexité d'une telle convalescence. Rester éloigné des terrains durant six mois sans certitude quant à la date exacte d'un retour s'avère extrêmement lourd à gérer sur le plan psychologique, à plus forte raison lorsque cela s'accompagne d'un rendez-vous manqué majeur comme une Coupe du monde et d'un changement d'environnement à assimiler. Bruno Genesio sur le retour en puissance de Nayef Aguerd : « On en revient toujours aux cas individuels. Nayef est resté six mois blessé et ne savait pas quandil allait reprendre. C'est très, très difficile à vivre mentalement. Il a raté une Coupe du monde, ce qui n'est pas… pic.twitter.com/mUwwCdfcLL — La Minute OM (@LaMinuteOM_) November 7, 2026 Bruno Genesio a tenu à saluer le travail du staff médical, dont l'accompagnement a été déterminant pour permettre au joueur de retrouver son plein potentiel physique. Ayant déjà eu le joueur sous ses ordres à Rennes par le passé, l'entraîneur retrouve aujourd'hui à Marseille un élément dont il connaît parfaitement le registre et les qualités fondamentales. Le coach a ainsi mis en avant le profil complet du Lion de l'Atlas, louant sa domination dans le jeu aérien, sa pointe de vitesse ainsi que sa finesse technique pour ressortir proprement le ballon depuis l'arrière. Au-delà de ses qualités athlétiques et techniques, l'international marocain s'impose comme un maillon fort du dispositif phocéen. Son expérience au plus haut niveau et sa sérénité constituent aujourd'hui des atouts précieux sur lesquels le staff marseillais compte s'appuyer pour consolider la charnière centrale de l'équipe. The post OM : Bruno Genesio salue le retour en force de Nayef Aguerd appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?
items.description: A hysterical map on social media has cooked up an image of the blast radius of radioactive fallout if Iran’s nuclear facilities were attacked. It fancies that it shows how radiation would reach Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, parts of Afghanistan, and potentially other areas depending on atmospheric conditions. The map is based on the claim that: ‘Pakistan and Afghanistan would be blanketed by the fallout of radiation if nuclear facilities in Iran are attacked.’ Such a broad conclusion reflects an incomplete understanding of the nature of Iran’s nuclear facilities as well as the geographical and metrological factors that would determine the potential consequences of any military strike. It should, therefore, be approached with caution and supported by a rigorous, evidence-based assessment instead of being presented as an inevitable outcome. In our view, this claim has been presented without real data, supporting facts, calculations, or illustrations of a plausible scenario or a string of scenarios resulting from any such attack of this nature. For it to be credible, certain assumptions would need to be established under two possibilities: an attack on facilities carrying fission fragments and irradiated fuel and, an attack on facilities carrying natural uranium, enriched uranium, heavy water, mining and milling facilities, research reactors etc. Then these two possibilities should be considered with the choice and the nature of the attacks if carried out by the United States and its allies. Let us examine two possible scenarios; in one conventional weapons are used and in the other nuclear weapons are used to attack Iran’s facilities. What are Iran’s facilities Natanz is the principal industrial uranium enrichment complex with underground and above-ground infrastructure. It has been hit by the US and its above-ground structures have been destroyed. The underground allegedly fissionable material is still unknown in quantity and enrichment capacity . Fordow is an underground uranium enrichment facility near Qum, recognized as an advanced enrichment installation located within a mountain complex. The facility has reportedly been struck repeatedly, however, no definitive confirmation has emerged regarding the American claim that it was destroyed, or that radiation plumes are expanding . The Isfahan Nuclear Complex is a uranium conversion and nuclear fuel fabrication facility. The Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant is a commercial VVER-1000 MW pressurized water reactor. A possible fallout if the attack is not restricted to Pakistan or Afghanistan, but will cover the entire Gulf region, including Saudi Arabia. The consequences would be similar to that of Chernobyl which demonstrated that radioactive fallout with highly variable contamination can be detected more than 1000km away. American bases and its allies can also suffer. The Tehran Research Complex is a 5MW research reactor that uses 20% enriched uranium as fuel. The Khondab Heavy Water Reactor is not a facility carrying fissionable materials. The uranium mining and processing facilities are non-fissionable material facilities in terms of radiation fallouts. Iran also possesses supporting facilities for nuclear research, centrifuge manufacturing, hot cells, and other related activities. But they cannot be considered facilities carrying fissionable materials that can lead to radiation fallouts that could reach Pakistan or Afghanistan. The American and Israeli military attacks in June 2025 affected several major Iranian nuclear facilities. Therefore, the list above should not be interpreted as a confirmation that all these installations are currently operational. These facilities do not present the same radiological hazards as operating nuclear power plants. Nevertheless, an assessment of the consequences of the previous attacks indicates that significant radioactive fallout was not detected beyond the affected facilities. Similarly, an attack on Natanz and Fordow would not necessarily result in significant radiological releases into the wider environment because uranium and enriched uranium, although radioactive, do not contain the substantial inventory of fission products found in irradiated reactor fuel. Significant contamination within a damaged enrichment facility is possible. However, a major radiological release affecting Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, or the UAE should not be considered a reasonable default assumption. The IAEA watchdog has already stated that following the June 2025 attacks, radiation levels outside the affected facilities remained normal. Therefore, claims regarding radiological consequences for neighbouring countries should not be based on unsupported assumptions. The situation would be considerably different in the case of a nuclear power plant operating along the Persian Gulf coast. If such a facility were struck by conventional weapons, the potential consequences could be more serious because it contains substantial quantities of radioactive fission products and irradiated nuclear fuel. Its geographical location, together with prevailing wind patterns, could also contribute to a wider radiological exposure and fallout pattern than would be expected from attacks on inland Iranian facilities, many of which are deeply buried or constructed with protective infrastructure in accordance with the safety requirements applicable to civilian nuclear installations. A severe accident involving damage to the reactor core, loss of cooling, or failure of safety barriers could release radioactive material. However, a projectile striking a nuclear power plant does not automatically mean that sufficient radioactive material will be released into the environment to cause a major radiological accident. The consequences would depend on whether the reactor, its safety systems, cooling systems, and supporting infrastructure were damaged, as well as the extent of that damage. Furthermore, attacks on civilian nuclear power plants raise serious issues under international humanitarian law and applicable international conventions, including the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material and Nuclear Facilities (as amended by the 2005 Amendment), 1977 Additional Protocol to the Geneva Convention etc. Any assessment of such an attack must also take into account whether the nuclear power plant is operational at the time of the strike. The most significant question is what military purpose will the United States gain from attacking a nuclear power plant which has been under the IAEA safeguards for decades and is not reported for any diversion of. nuclear materials from the facility. Other nuclear facilities, including research reactors, fuel fabrication plants, uranium conversion facilities, and radioactive material storage locations, may also present some risk of radiological releases. However, these risks are considerably smaller than those associated with a large operating nuclear power plant in terms of radiation fallouts or contamination zones. The overall assessment of the potential consequences for each facility is as follows: Natanz / Fordow enrichment plants : Low radiological consequences beyond the immediate facility, with no reasonable basis for assuming a significant radiological threat to neighboring countries. Isfahan conversion/fuel facilities : Primarily localized chemical and radiological hazards are expected. Research reactors : Potential radiological consequences that would generally be expected to remain within a limited geographical area, potentially extending a few kilometers from the facility, depending on the nature and severity of the incident. Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant and spent fuel storage: Potentially serious transboundary radiological consequences in the event of a severe accident, although such an outcome is not inevitable and would depend on the nature and extent of the damage. What if you go nuclear? Another scenario sometimes discussed is the possibility of using nuclear weapons against Iran or its nuclear facilities. This remains highly speculative and extremely unlikely. Nuclear weapons have been used in warfare only once, in 1945, when the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Since then, despite numerous international conflicts, severe geopolitical crises, and periods of heightened nuclear tensions, no country has resorted to using nuclear weapons in an armed conflict. This restraint reflects the understanding of not only the devastating humanitarian and environmental consequences of their use but also the far-reaching strategic, political, and international repercussions that would inevitably follow. Most importantly, the use of nuclear weapons would not necessarily translate into a military victory for the United States. On the contrary, it could result in a complete loss of control over the Strait of Hormuz as the region may not approve of such an action. Already the US has achieved successful engagement of its military targets at the very onset of the war. And lastly Bushrer does not qualify as a significant military target. Iran’s demonstrated resilience in maintaining its political and military structures during and after the initial strikes against its leadership and strategic installations indicates that the projection of a decisive military victory cannot be sustained unilaterally. Any eventual political settlement would still require the acceptance of the Iranian leadership, which may not be forthcoming. The use of nuclear weapons against Iran would cross an exceptionally dangerous threshold. It would fundamentally alter the international security environment, undermine the longstanding norm against nuclear weapons use, and potentially trigger unpredictable regional and global consequences. The country responsible could face enormous international condemnation, diplomatic isolation, and potentially severe strategic repercussions. This would be an extremely difficult and potentially self-defeating course of action, particularly when a range of conventional military, diplomatic, economic, and other alternatives remain available. Why would any country deliberately do this when the consequences could extend far beyond the immediate conflict and potentially shape international security for generations to come? In our assessment, the use of nuclear weapons should therefore be treated as an extreme hypothetical scenario rather than a realistic expectation in the context of the current confrontation. It is scientifically inappropriate to assume that damage to Iranian uranium enrichment and nuclear fuel-cycle facilities would necessarily expose neighbouring countries to significant levels of radiation. Serious questions can be raised about American professor, Robert A. Pape’s warning that Pakistan and Afghanistan would inevitably face severe radiological consequences ( watch this influencer’s Urdu commentary ). Such an assessment would require a detailed understanding of the specific facility targeted, its operational status, the radioactive inventory involved, the nature and extent of the damage, and the prevailing meteorological conditions and also the war outcome. Significant transboundary radiological fallout cannot simply be presumed; it would require a credible scientific assessment supported by facility-specific data and atmospheric dispersion modelling. A deep understanding is needed of the war objectives of the United States whether they can be achieved by the use of nuclear weapons. The same is true for Israeli military planners as well, except in this case the Iranian ability to respond would perhaps create a new phase of a war cycle which would not be as controllable as believed. A nuclear war is too serious a business to be left for the arbitrary conclusions where it can affect the future of mankind itself.

items.title: « Faure dreams batissons ensemble » : le ministère des finances dénonce une escroquerie
items.description: Lomé, 6 nov. (ATOP) – Dans une vidéo relayée ces derniers jours sur les réseaux sociaux, une association dénommée « Faure Dreams, Bâtissons Ensemble », propose des tontines à partir d’un montant de 100 FCFA par jour, avec distribution gratuite de carnet. Dans un communiqué rendu public le vendredi 6 novembre, le ministre des Finances et du budget informe l’opinion publique que ces agissements s’assimilent à des escroqueries à grande échelle et à visage découvert. Selon le communiqué, les initiateurs promettent d’aider les personnes désireuses d’obtenir, dans les meilleurs délais, des pièces telles que le jugement supplétif, le certificat de nationalité, la carte nationale d’identité ou le passeport. Le ministre rappelle que la collecte de dépôts est une activité réglementée qui ne peut être exercée sans autorisation. « Des recherches menées, il ressort que l’association dénommée « Faure Dreams, Bätissons Ensemble » n’est ni agréée, ni inscrite sur la liste des institutions de microfinance. Elle n’est donc pas en règle et ne peut, en aucun cas, collecter l’épargne des populations. Elle n’est liée, ni mandatée par aucun service public ou la Présidence du Conseil », indique le communiqué. Par conséquent, le ministre appelle la population à une plus grande vigilance, surtout en cette période de fin d’année. Il signale que des dispositions sont d’ores et déjà en cours pour interpeller les initiateurs de cette vidéo. Le ministre saisit cette occasion pour mettre en garde, une fois encore, les auteurs de ces manœuvres frauduleuses qu’ils s’exposent à la rigueur de la loi. Il réitère son engagement à protéger les citoyens contre ces arnaques et demeure disponible pour toutes informations complémentaires. ATOP/Communiqué du ministère des finances et du budget

items.title: Oti/éducation : 269 élèves-professeurs entament leur formation à l’ENFPE de Mango
items.description: Mango, 7 nov. (ATOP) – Deux cent soixante-neuf Elèves-professeurs d’école (EPE) de la 5 è promotion (2026-2028) de l’Ecole normale de formation des professeurs d’écoles (ENFPE) de Mango ont entamé leur formation, le jeudi 5 novembre. La formation s’étend sur deux ans, répartis en quatre semestres. Elle comprend des enseignements théoriques, ainsi que des stages pratiques dans les structures préscolaires. Lors de la cérémonie d’accueil, les nouveaux apprenants ont suivi une conférence inaugurale sur le thème « Le professionnalisme, l’excellence et les valeurs citoyennes, socle de compétences du professeur d’école », animée par le directeur adjoint de l’ENFPE de Mango, Koega Minisimabéseo. Celui-ci a exhorté les futurs enseignants à actualiser régulièrement leurs connaissances, à faire preuve de professionnalisme et à cultiver les valeurs de discipline, de tolérance et de paix. Il a souligné qu’ils doivent être des modèles pour les enfants et leur communauté. La nouvelle promotion a pris également connaissance du programme de formation, des différentes unités d’enseignement et des stages pratiques. Ils ont été sensibilisés aux exigences du métier, notamment l’assiduité, la ponctualité, la discipline et la recherche de l’excellence. Le directeur de l’ENFPE de Mango, Ayissa Komi Wola, représentant le ministre de l’Education nationale, a indiqué que la formation des enseignants constitue un levier essentiel pour garantir une éducation de qualité, conformément aux objectifs du Plan sectoriel de l’éducation (PSE) et aux Objectifs de développement durable (ODD). Il les a invités à faire preuve d’assiduité, de détermination et d’abnégation tout au long de leur formation. Pour sa part, le secrétaire général de la préfecture de l’Oti, N’Gbamou Koya, a exhorté les apprenants à faire preuve d’engagement et de comportement exemplaire. Il a également invité les formateurs à accompagner efficacement les futurs enseignants dans l’acquisition des compétences professionnelles et des valeurs indispensables à l’exercice de leur métier. M. N’Gbamou a réaffirmé la disponibilité des autorités locales à soutenir l’établissement. La porte-parole de la promotion, Mlle Namougou Kamboaloa, a salué les efforts du gouvernement en faveur de la formation des enseignants et promis l’engagement de tous les apprenants à travailler pour réussir leur parcours. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence du maire de la commune Oti 1, Noukome Nimani Ignace et du commissaire de la ville de Mango, Agboh Koffi. Outre la cérémonie d’accueil, douze EPE de la 3 è promotion, ayant bénéficié d’une formation en ligne en anglais, organisée par l’ambassade des USA au Togo, ont reçu leurs diplômes de fin de formation. L’ambiance a été entretenue par la chorale de l’école. ATOP/TT/JK/AR

items.title: Mike Johnson Will Tend To Your Lawn Now
items.description: “Heaven forbid, if we lose this majority or whatever, I don’t know what my next chapter of life is, I’m just open to it. And if God moves on our hearts and says we should, you know, go back to my hometown of Shreveport and start a lawn business, I’ll do that with equal fervor. I mean, I just want to be of my highest and best use to God and to my country.” — Mike Johnson, to Fox News’s Aishah Hasnie Mike Johnson finished his circuit of the lawn on his riding mower, dismounted, and stared at the tree. It was an old tree, large and ornamental. Yet something about the branches was wrong. But what? If only he could ask Donald Trump for advice! No—this was his new job, his lawn-care business. It was going to be a lot more work than he had anticipated. There should be more jobs like speaker of the House, without any major responsibilities except to sit at the feet of the president and gaze at him in silent adoration. Now Johnson felt like he was working all the time. And, worse, he had to direct his own activities. But after losing the majority, he had been left with no choice. He could not seek election to the minority leadership. Minority leadership? That smacked of DEI. The lawns of Shreveport needed him, and he would answer. The biggest question had been what to call the business. Finally, he decided on Mike Johnson Total Landscaping, an homage to his former patron. It was hard to figure out how to begin without Trump’s guiding hand. He knew some things about Trump’s attitude toward lawns, but not all. Grass, he knew, had a life , like people. And trees were bad. Trees were the enemy. To cut down 400 trees as quickly as possible was a great act. Pools were generally good—some, but not others. He had made notes of all of this, but there were still so many blanks to fill in. Were grassroots movements good or bad? How could you tell if something was a weed? It was hard to think for himself after so many months out of practice. Occasionally he thought of the time when he had been speaker of the House. What a strange time! It almost felt like a dream. What a strange job, too. He had understood that the speaker of the House was third in line to the presidency, and therefore it behooved him to remain in careful seclusion from any kind of disturbing news , so that if he were called upon to serve, he would be rested and ready. Yet people were always asking him frustrating questions, as though he were meant to be keeping up on things, approving or disapproving of events, or even taking an active role in them. But he had known better: His purpose was to serve the president. Such a funny title, given that! “Speaker of the House.” He wondered what house it was. The White House, maybe. Since leaving that role, he’d had much more time to catch up on news. Astounding how much had happened in the country since he left Shreveport! He had been wondering why he saw so few other landscapers. He heard from his friends at Greenwater Services that there had been some roving gangs of masked men making people frightened to leave home. He also heard that there was a war of some kind? Gasoline was certainly expensive, but he had to keep his mower running somehow. Now that he had finally caught up on all the news, he’d started listening to a book on tape: the U.S. Constitution. What he’d learned disturbed him. “Did you know about this?” he had asked his wife, at the end of his first day trimming hedges. “What?” “Apparently, there are three equal branches of government. Congress is actually the first one mentioned. Before the president, even. Article I!” He frowned. “I had no idea. Equal branches.” “What do you think it means?” she said. She sounded worried. He’d kept listening. “Did you know?” he said, the next afternoon. “The leader of that equal branch of government—do you know what that job is called?” She shook her head. “The speaker of the House,” he said. “Isn’t that funny?” She frowned. “But that’s the same name as your old job,” she said. It was a strange coincidence, he thought. Nothing more. Still, sometimes, he wondered. Now he stared at the tree. Something was the matter with its branches, but he did not know what to do to fix it. Cut the strong one? Cut the weak one, maybe? If only Donald Trump were here. He would be sure to know what to do.

items.title: Americans Are Spending Less Time With Friends
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. What does your ideal night look like? Maybe it’s dinner with friends or a quiet evening at home with family or a partner. If you picked the latter option, you are part of a growing contingent of Americans who are spending less time with friends and, by some measures, more time with family. Although enjoying the company of loved ones can be deeply fulfilling, something may be lost when our household makes up the majority of our social life. In a recent Atlantic story, my colleague Faith Hill explores why friendship is taking a back seat to family time. In one survey, nearly 40 percent of respondents who said they wished they saw friends more cited a lack of money as an obstacle; others pointed to busy schedules and exhaustion. “More Americans are hanging out with family—by choice, but also by necessity,” Faith writes. Friendships offer a type of companionship that family life can’t always provide. But unlike family ties, friendships depend on our continued attention to nurture them, making them meaningful—and easier to lose. The Socializing That’s Replacing Friend Time By Faith Hill More Americans are hanging out with family—by choice, but also by necessity. Read the article. The Friendship Paradox By Olga Khazan We all want more time with our friends, but we’re spending more time alone. ( From 2024 ) Read the article. What If Friendship, Not Marriage, Was at the Center of Life? By Rhaina Cohen “Our boyfriends, our significant others, and our husbands are supposed to be No. 1. Our worlds are backward.” ( From 2020 ) Read the article. Still Curious? Another symptom of growing isolation : A recent study found that people spoke fewer words a day in 2019 than in 2005, Olga Khazan wrote. The new age of endless parenting : More grown kids are in near-constant contact with their family. Some call this a failure to launch—but there’s another way to look at it, Hill wrote in 2024. Other Diversions The school apps are out of control. LeBron James, Philadelphian An underrated reason boys are reading less PS Courtesy of Allie S. My colleague Isabel Fattal recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. “Where I live is often crispy and dry by early summer; everything loses its greenness and turns golden to brown. But a week or so ago we got some great rain, so I moseyed down to the river, to a spot I frequent often, and was enamored by the vibrant pops of green lichen and moss on the boulders and trees next to the river,” Allie S. from El Portal, California, shared. “The contrasting textures and colors were an absolute delight. And there is something truly special about returning to a place again and again and then one day seeing it in a new way and appreciating it once more.” We’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Rafaela

items.title: Face à l’inflation, les Marocains contraints de serrer encore la ceinture
items.description: La crise qui frappe l'économie marocaine déteint fatalement sur la situation sociale déjà très précaire de larges franges de la population. Les Marocains ont dû serrer davantage la ceinture, comme l'indiquent les chiffres officiels et les constatations sur le terrain. Les trois quarts des ménages marocains ont ressenti une baisse de leur niveau de vie Selon une enquête du Haut-Commissariat au plan (HCP) publiée à la mi-octobre, 76,3 % des ménages marocains ont indiqué que leurs conditions de vie se sont dégradées pendant ces 12 derniers mois. La proportion de ceux qui estiment que leur niveau de vie n’a pas bougé est de 18,5 %, tandis que seulement 5,2 % ont constaté une amélioration. Pour couvrir leurs dépenses, 39 % des ménages marocains ont dit qu'ils sont contraints de recourir à l’emprunt ou de puiser dans leur épargne. La proportion de ceux qui parviennent encore à épargner est infime : à peine 2,8 %. Et l’heure n’est pas à l’optimisme, puisque plus de la moitié (51,7 %) des ménages marocains sondés ont indiqué qu’ils prévoient une dégradation de leurs conditions dans les 12 prochains mois, contre 39,6 % qui s'attendent à un maintien et 8,7 % qui entrevoient une amélioration de leur situation, tandis que 61,3 % des familles anticipent une hausse du taux de chômage. L’enquête a fait ressortir une baisse de l’indice de confiance des ménages (ICM) par rapport au deuxième trimestre de l’année, passant de 60,1 à 59,2 points. Maroc : Hausse vertigineuse des prix des produits alimentaires L’inflation qui frappe le Maroc touche tous les produits, notamment les carburants et les produits alimentaires. D'ailleurs, presque la totalité (95,9 %) des ménages interrogés dans le cadre de l'enquête du HCP jugent que les prix des produits alimentaires ont augmenté. Cette hausse des prix est constatée par le média Al Arabiya lors d’une virée dans un marché marocain. De nombreux témoignages recueillis ont confirmé qu'il est de plus en plus difficile de joindre les deux bouts. « Personne n’arrive à boucler les fins de mois », déclare un père de famille proche de la retraite qui se plaint, par exemple, du fait que les prix de la tomate aient atteint 15 dirhams le kilogramme. Les prix de la viande ont aussi flambé, passant de 70-80 dirhams à 150, voire 250 dirhams. « Les clients ont réduit leurs achats, ils achètent parfois un demi-kilogramme de légumes », assure un commerçant. Le Maroc, un pays vulnérable aux fluctuations du marché mondial Le Maroc est l’un des pays les plus vulnérables aux crises et aux dysfonctionnements du marché international. Les fortes inégalités font que les répercussions de l’inflation s'abattent sur les couches défavorisées qui constituent l'essentiel de la population. Les données publiées en octobre dernier ont fait état du recul de la valeur du dirham par rapport au dollar de 6,5 % depuis fin juillet. Dans le même temps, la valeur des importations s'est envolée, se répercutant directement sur les réserves en devises du pays et le pouvoir d'achat. Pour ne rien arranger, la crise au Moyen-Orient a frappé de plein fouet la filière phosphates, tandis que le rythme de croissance du secteur du tourisme a fortement ralenti. Tout cela se produit alors que le royaume dépense sans compter en armements israéliens et dans la réalisation d’infrastructures de prestige en prévision de la Coupe du monde 2030. L’article Face à l'inflation, les Marocains contraints de serrer encore la ceinture est apparu en premier sur TSA .

Irene Montero llama a secundar la huelga en su presentación con Rufián en Madrid: “Hay que paralizar el país”
items.description: El atuendo de él, tan comentado en el primer acto conjunto hace dos semanas en Barcelona , permite a Gabriel Rufián comenzar su discurso con una broma: “Hoy había que ir de amarillo. Así de conectados estamos, porque esto no lo habíamos hablado. Amarillo de ERC, ya la hemos fichado totalmente”, dice mirando a Irene Montero, que lleva un jersey de idéntico color al suyo. Los cabezas de lista de Podemos y ERC a las generales del 29-N han presentado este sábado a mediodía su propuesta política en el corazón de Madrid con alusiones a la actualidad, como la huelga general por la vivienda o la corrupción. “El 11 de noviembre hay que llenar las calles y hay que paralizar el país para que bajen los alquileres, los alimentos y la energía”, ha arengado la candidata a cuatro días de la convocatoria. Seguir leyendo Colau pide un "vuelco" como el de Lula en Brasil La candidata de Frente Amplio, Ada Colau, ha llamado este sábado a una movilización masiva de la izquierda para "dar la vuelta a las encuestas" de cara a las próximas elecciones. Durante un acto en el barrio barcelonés de Sant Andreu, la exalcaldesa de la ciudad ha asegurado que su candidatura roza el 8% en intención de voto y se ha marcado el objetivo de alcanzar el 10%, cifra que, según sus cálculos, permitiría duplicar la representación parlamentaria actual y restar escaños a Vox. Colau ha apelado al ejemplo de Lula da Silva en Brasil para reivindicar la capacidad de la movilización popular de alterar los pronósticos electorales: "La última palabra la tiene la gente, el pueblo, los barrios y la mayoría social trabajadora". En materia económica, Colau ha defendido un aumento de la presión fiscal sobre las rentas más altas para reforzar la financiación de la sanidad y la educación públicas. La candidata también ha situado la vivienda entre las prioridades de su programa y ha planteado la "expropiación de pisos a los fondos buitre" si las fuerzas progresistas consiguen revalidar el Gobierno central tras el 29N.

items.title: Labé : armé d’un couteau, un jeune tente d’agresser un imam de Tata 2 en pleine prière
items.description: Une scène de panique s’est produite ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026 dans la mosquée de Yérandé, située au quartier Tata 2, dans la commune urbaine de Labé. En pleine prière du vendredi, un jeune homme muni d’un couteau aurait tenté de s’en prendre au deuxième imam de la mosquée, alors que celui-ci dirigeait l’office religieux. Selon les informations recueillies, les faits se sont déroulés aux environs de 13 h 40. Le jeune homme, présenté comme un élève d’une école coranique située à proximité, aurait fait irruption dans la mosquée avant de se diriger vers le mihrab, où se trouvait l’imam. La réaction rapide des muezzins présents aux côtés de l’imam a permis d’éviter le pire. L’un d’eux aurait réussi à intercepter et à maîtriser le jeune homme, avec le concours de certains responsables du quartier. La prière a ensuite pu se poursuivre normalement. Joint au téléphone, Mamadou Mouctar Diallo, adjoint au président du conseil de quartier de Tata 2, a confirmé les faits et apporté des précisions sur les circonstances de l’incident. « Par la grâce de Dieu, l’acte n’est pas allé à son terme. C’est aux environs de 13 h 40, au moment de la prière, qu’un jeune inscrit dans une école coranique tout près de chez nous est venu armé d’un couteau. Il a foncé vers le mihrab. Heureusement, le deuxième muezzin l’a bloqué et l’a ceinturé avec force », a-t-il expliqué. Notre interlocuteur affirme également que le jeune homme aurait auparavant proféré des menaces à l’encontre de l’imam. Selon son témoignage, le mis en cause aurait exprimé son intention de l’éliminer, estimant que c’était à lui de lui succéder. Il précise que le cheikh du jeune aurait auparavant pris des engagements pour assurer sa surveillance, mais que ces dispositions n’auraient pas été respectées. Alertés, les services de sécurité, notamment la gendarmerie, se sont rendus sur les lieux. À l’issue des échanges entre les responsables du quartier et le cheikh du jeune, ce dernier aurait pris l’engagement de conduire son élève à Conakry afin qu’il bénéficie d’une prise en charge médicale. Selon les informations recueillies, le jeune mis en cause aurait finalement été conduit vers la capitale pour une évaluation de son état de santé mentale. Cet incident suscite de nombreuses réactions au sein de la population de Labé. Aucune communication officielle n’a toutefois été faite concernant d’éventuelles poursuites judiciaires ou les conclusions de la prise en charge médicale. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : armé d’un couteau, un jeune tente d’agresser un imam de Tata 2 en pleine prière est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: After midterm rout, Vance tries to build his own 2028 brand
items.description: Late in his blitz to salvage Republicans’ midterm fortunes, Vice President JD Vance shifted strategy. He talked less about President Donald Trump and more about the issues that define his own political identity. Vance argued the case for Republicans, who lost control of Congress in Tuesday’s vote , almost exclusively through the lens of his policy portfolio, according to a Reuters review of half a dozen speeches since the Republican convention in September. He bypassed Trump’s signature policies, including the Iran war and deportations , as polls showed the president’s sagging popularity dragging down Republican office-seekers. The change was deliberate, according to two people familiar with the strategy. Vance and his advisers saw the issues he championed — economic nationalism, foreign policy restraint and public safety as politically potent subjects he could address with authority. While Trump embraced them as part of his ‘Make America Great Again’ (MAGA) movement, Vance had emerged as their lead crusader, the people said. The shift offered an early glimpse of how the 42-year-old vice president could chart his own course as Republicans begin looking beyond Trump. Vance hasn’t said whether he will run for president in 2028, and Trump hasn’t endorsed him or anyone else. But Vance is viewed as a leading potential contender who some Republican officials say will need to inherit much of Trump’s coalition while separating himself from his boss’s baggage. Vance took a more public step on Wednesday toward reinforcing his own political brand with an unusually blunt election postmortem. In a social media post, he blamed the Iran war for Republicans’ midterm defeat and laid out a platform for a Republican rebound. He called for a swift end to the conflict and urged Republicans to focus on affordability, reevaluate foreign relations and overhaul the US relationship with Israel. Trump has called Americans’ affordability concerns a Democratic hoax. He launched a war against Iran following sustained lobbying from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Trump went on to endorse Netanyahu in the Israeli election. Vance makes unease at the war public The post, for the first time, put Vance openly on the side of ending the war. Three people familiar with the White House and Vance’s communications told Reuters that the vice president was not breaking with Trump and said White House chief of staff Susie Wiles knew in advance about Vance’s post. On Friday, Trump reshuffled senior White House leadership, replacing Wiles with Stephen Miller in a move that suggests the White House plans to double down on some of Trump’s more hardline policies. Trump has acknowledged the Iran war played a role in the Republican rout because of the resulting high gas prices but has continued to defend it. “I would have done nothing different,” he told reporters on Wednesday. A plume of smoke rises after a US-Israeli strike as loud explosions were heard in the central and eastern parts of the Iranian capital, Tehran on March 3, 2026. — AFP/File Reuters could not determine whether Trump was aware of the post in advance. Donald Trump Jr, the president’s eldest son, endorsed Vance’s remarks on social media, along with some conservative allies. The dialogue further elevated Vance as a potential post-Trump conservative standard-bearer, said Michael Ricci, a Republican strategist and former adviser to House Speakers John Boehner and Paul Ryan. Using the megaphone of the vice presidency He said Vance’s message forced conservatives to debate the merits of the war, and more broadly, what core tenets Republican presidential candidates should embrace in 2028. “It’s simplistic to say this about him looking for ways to differentiate himself from Trump,” Ricci said. “This is about him using his megaphone of the vice presidency to set the terms of debate.” Representatives for Vance declined to comment. White House representatives referred Reuters to Trump’s comments on Wednesday, when he told reporters he understood Vance’s perspective on the election results. US Vice President JD Vance arrives to speak at a midterm campaign rally on October 28, 2026 in Kinston, North Carolina, the US. — Reuters Democrats are poised to tie Vance or any Republican nominee to Trump in 2028, especially if Trump plays a large role in vetting conservative hopefuls. “There’s a real challenge of how you position yourself to be viable in a general election while winning a primary that still requires you to bow down and kiss the ring, said Igor Volsky, a Democratic strategist. Vance’s brand did not emerge from the midterms unscathed. Republicans lost in states where he campaigned. Some of the strategies he endorsed, including an ad by Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that cast doubt on the sexual abuse suffered by the victorious Democratic candidate, Amy Acton, may have swung races away from Republicans. Other possible 2028 presidential contenders have offered their diagnoses of the midterm defeat. Texas Senator Ted Cruz said Republicans hadn’t done enough on affordability. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said losing candidates had focused too heavily on transgender issues and neglected voter concerns about data centres and artificial intelligence. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stayed silent. Vance’s effort to shape the debate was visible during the closing days of the campaign. In stump speeches, he told voters to support Republicans because they would investigate fraud in federal health care and antipoverty programs, tying that to the White House’s immigration agenda and cost of living. He almost entirely ignored the Iran war and gas prices, and seldom mentioned Trump by name. “I want my kids to raise a family in a country that is vibrant and thriving and free and prosperous. I want the simple things,” Vance said at one of his final rallies in North Carolina. “And because I want that for me, I want it for you too.”

items.title: La Tunisie embourbée dans le problème des migrants irréguliers
items.description: La Tunisie officielle rejette l’idée de faire du pays un territoire d’accueil permanent pour les migrants en situation irrégulière en route vers l’Europe. Sauf qu’en réalité, la Tunisie est en passe de devenir un territoire de transit ou d’installation pour beaucoup de migrants irréguliers, notamment subsahariens, généralement entrés par les frontières algériennes et libyennes. Ce qui pose des problèmes sécuritaires et sociaux et alimente la colère d’un bon nombre de Tunisiens, notamment les plus démunis, qui pensent, non sans raison, que la présence de ces personnes – dont les autorités évitent d’estimer le nombre réel – aggrave la situation économique et sociale dans un pays déjà en crise. (Photo : Pour quelques milliers de migrants irréguliers retournés chez eux, combien entrent chaque jour au pays et combien dépensent l'argent que leur donne l'OIM et reviennent par les mêmes voies?) Imed Bahri La Tunisie continuera à lutter contre les réseaux criminels impliqués dans le trafic de migrants et la traite des êtres humains, a déclaré le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Migration et des Tunisiens à l’étranger, Mohamed Ali Nafti, lors d’une réunion conjointe des commissions parlementaires de l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) et du Conseil national des régions et des districts (CNRD), vendredi 6 novembre 2026, consacrée à l’examen du budget de son ministère pour 2027, réaffirmant au passage le refus du pays de devenir un pays de transit ou d’installation pour les migrants en situation irrégulière, ou encore une plateforme de débarquement pour les migrants et les demandeurs d’asile. Le chef de la diplomatie tunisienne a réaffirmé la détermination du gouvernement à défendre la souveraineté nationale, à protéger les frontières et à combattre les organisations criminelles qui exploitent les flux migratoires. Il a toutefois souligné que la politique migratoire tunisienne repose sur une approche globale intégrant les dimensions humanitaires, économiques, sociales et de développement, dans le respect de la dignité et des droits des migrants. Selon les données communiquées par les autorités tunisiennes lors d'une rencontre entre M. Nafti et la directrice générale de l’OIM, Amy Pope, à New York le 22 septembre dernier, 5 077 retours volontaires avaient été enregistrés depuis le début de l’année 2026 dans le cadre du mécanisme d’assistance et de réintégration. Cela porte à 25 351 le nombre total de bénéficiaires du programme, sans compter les retours effectués via des vols commerciaux réguliers. Migrants subsahariens l Ce que la Tunisie refuse de voir Pour quelques départs, combien d'entrées ? La position exprimée par le ministre s’inscrit dans la ligne politique du président Kaïs Saïed, qui rejette l’idée de faire de la Tunisie un territoire d’accueil permanent pour les migrants en situation irrégulière en route vers l’Europe. Sauf que la lutte contre la migration irrégulière en empêchant les migrants de rejoindre les côtes européennes, si elle baisse les flux de leurs arrivées sur les côtes italiennes, elle ne sert pas les intérêts de la Tunisie, qui se trouve submergée, du nord au sud, de l'est à l'ouest, dans pratiquement toutes les villes côtières, par une population qu’elle n’a pas les moyens de nourrir, d’abriter, d’éduquer et de soigner… Ne nous voilons pas la face : pour quelques milliers de migrants irréguliers retournés chez eux, combien entrent chaque jour au pays et combien dépensent l'argent du retour que leur donne l'OIM et reviennent à notre pays par les mêmes voies? En d'autres termes, les gesticulations ne règlent pas les problèmes; elles servent parfois à cacher la réalité qu'elles dénoncent. N'est-ce pas M. Nafti ? L’article La Tunisie embourbée dans le problème des migrants irréguliers est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Pakistan, Sudan sign visa-free travel agreement for official, diplomatic passport holders
items.description: Pakistan and Sudan on Saturday signed an agreement on visa-free travel for official and diplomatic passport holders, according to a statement by the Ministry of Interior. “Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Sudanese Interior Minister Lt Gen Babiker Samra Mustafa Ali signed the agreement,” the ministry said on the social media platform X. “Under the agreement, holders of Pakistani and Sudanese official and diplomatic passports will be able to enter each other’s countries without a visa,” it stated. “Both interior ministers welcomed the visa-free entry agreement for official and diplomatic passports,” the statement said. “This agreement marks an important milestone in bilateral relations between Pakistan and Sudan,” it added. The statement emphasised that the visa-free facility would further facilitate high-level contacts and exchanges of delegations between Pakistan and Sudan. “New opportunities will emerge to promote official-level ties and mutual cooperation between the two countries.” “The agreement will further strengthen friendly relations and institutional cooperation between Pakistan and Sudan, the Sudanese interior minister was quoted as saying. “Both interior ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further consolidating and strengthening bilateral relations,” the statement added. Earlier on Saturday, both countries also decided to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to enhance cooperation in combating cybercrime, the statement by the interior ministry said. The decision was taken during delegation-level talks between interior ministers of both countries. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also attended the meeting. The Sudanese interior minister said his country wanted to benefit from Pakistan’s expertise and experience in combating cybercrime, the statement said. “The two sides also agreed to expand cooperation in security, internal affairs, police training, institutional cooperation, the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) and other sectors.” “Pakistan is ready to extend all possible cooperation to Sudan in peace-building and reconstruction,” Naqvi was quoted as saying. “Pakistan is also ready to provide professional training to Sudanese police officers,” the interior minister said during the meeting. Briefing the visiting minister, Naqvi said that with Nadra’s cooperation, 36 million citizenship cards, 9 million national identity cards, 18 million birth certificates and 500,000 death certificates had been issued in Sudan. He said Nadra was ready to continue cooperation in the civil registration process. On a query by the Sudanese minister, Naqvi ordered immediate resolution of visa issues faced by married Sudanese women in Pakistan, the statement said. “Sudanese citizens can avail medical facilities in Pakistan and will be provided every possible facility in the health sector,” Naqvi said. “Pakistan is a brotherly country and Sudan attaches great importance to cooperation with it in all fields,” the Sudanese interior minister was quoted as saying. He expressed the desire to promote cooperation in various sectors and thanked Pakistan for its cooperation. A day ago, the Sudanese interior minister held a meeting with Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and discussed avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation between their countries. On Thursday, he also met Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif. In a meeting with the prime minister, he commended Pakistan’s support on international forums regarding efforts to restore peace and security in Sudan.

items.title: What Happened to JetBlue?
items.description: For airlines in the United States, going bankrupt is practically a rite of passage. Since the airline industry was deregulated almost 50 years ago, dozens of airlines have filed for Chapter 11, including each of the so-called Big Three carriers—United, American, and Delta. A notable exception has been JetBlue, which until recently was one of the industry’s few success stories. But after The Wall Street Journal reported last month that the airline’s mounting debt obligations moved senior creditors to hire restructuring advisers, some investors began assuming that bankruptcy was on the way. JetBlue’s CEO, Joanna Geraghty, insists otherwise. On the company’s most recent earnings call, in late October, she at least temporarily assuaged investor anxieties with claims that the airline was not at risk of going under, and was on track to return to profitability next year. Even so, JetBlue is undoubtedly struggling. The carrier has lost more than $3 billion since 2019, the last year it turned a full-year profit, and its debt load has risen swiftly to about $8.4 billion. The proximate cause of the company’s current woes is obvious: Fuel costs have soared since the Iran war began. But the challenge the company faces is more fundamental than that. JetBlue has been struggling because it finds itself in what’s sometimes called the “mushy middle,” caught between discount airlines on the low end and the big legacy carriers, which have lots of expense-account-wielding business travelers and lucrative transatlantic routes, on the high end. [ Read: An SNL sketch to make airlines feel ashamed ] When JetBlue began flying, in 2000, being in between was a strength: The company explicitly positioned itself as a stylish and plucky alternative to the ultra-low-cost carriers and the legacy carriers. It offered more legroom, good snacks, free satellite television, and leather seats to every customer, but still managed to be significantly cheaper than the big airlines. It was able to pull this off because its jet fleet was made up of only one type of plane, which kept maintenance costs down, and its workforce was not unionized. The carrier also initially offered just one class of seat, which helped it maximize space, even with the extra legroom.JetBlue’s marketing leaned into the idea that the company offered a new model for the industry, promising to “bring humanity back to air travel.” The carrier was so successful so quickly that legacy airlines tried to adopt this model for themselves: Delta and United started lower-cost, would-be JetBlue competitors in the 2000s, but both quickly failed. Meanwhile, JetBlue expanded its relatively low-cost, high-value offerings; in 2014, it launched a premium cabin for transcontinental routes called Mint, featuring lie-flat seats and fares well below those of the big carriers. By the late 2010s, it was the fifth-biggest airline in the country. Over much of the past decade, though, that sweet spot in the market that JetBlue had made its own has shrunk. On the low end, new discount airlines have sprung up, offering no frills but also very cheap fares. On the higher end, the legacy carriers have gotten better at exploiting their lucrative revenue sources, jacking up prices on business travel and transatlantic routes, and using their giant customer bases to partner with credit-card companies willing to pay them billions. JetBlue has found it hard to keep up. Even if the carrier had wanted to slash prices to compete with the discounters, its costs are now far too high for it to do so. Those jets that were brand-new when the company launched are aging, driving up maintenance costs, and its workforce began unionizing in 2014, driving up labor costs. (It also does not want to give up on the premium amenities that have made it so distinctive.) At the same time, JetBlue has struggled to compete with the legacy carriers for more profitable business travelers because most of its planes lack business- or first-class cabins, and the company doesn’t fly to nearly as many cities as the legacy carriers do. Nor has it been able to leverage its loyalty program, TrueBlue, the way the big carriers have leveraged theirs. TrueBlue will generate about $1 billion in revenue for the airline this year, which seems impressive until you realize that Delta makes more than $8 billion annually from the SkyMiles credit cards issued by American Express. [ Read: The only thing worse than Spirit Airlines ] These problems are in some respects specific to the airline industry. But JetBlue’s troubles are also emblematic of a basic fact about American business, which is that it has simply become harder for companies targeting the middle of the market to succeed. Traditional department stores such as Macy’s and Kohl’s have found themselves squeezed between big-box retailers and e-tailers such as Walmart, Target, and Amazon on the low end and premium retailers on the high end. Casual sit-down restaurants including Applebee’s and TGI Fridays have gotten edged out by fast-casual restaurants and fine dining. The disappearance of the American-made passenger car is also part of this story: Cars such as the Chrysler Sebring and the Chevy Malibu weren’t cheap enough, relative to their perceived level of quality, to compete with the perennially reliable Toyota Camry and Honda Accord, but they also weren’t fancy enough to compete with Lexus and Tesla. Consumers have become more price-conscious and are better informed about quality and cachet. So offering a pretty-good option at an almost-premium price doesn’t cut it anymore. JetBlue is not doomed. It still has valuable assets, including most notably its brand, which remains surprisingly strong—even if it’s now doing many of the things that annoy people about traditional airlines, such as raising baggage fees. Its planes still have more legroom and free Wi-Fi. And next month, the carrier is going to be rolling out first-class cabins on many of its domestic routes, which should boost revenue. When fuel costs come down, the company may well turn a profit again. But being JetBlue is never going to be easy. It’s stuck in the middle, and these days, that’s the toughest place for a business to be.

items.title: ICE After the Blowout
items.description: “D eportations will continue,” Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin wrote in a post on X the day after voters punished his party in the midterm election. The three-word statement appeared to be aimed at quieting an incipient debate among Republicans over whether President Trump should ease his ICE crackdown. Two years after he won back the White House promising the largest mass-deportation campaign in U.S. history, Trump and his party suffered monumental losses in states such as Texas, Georgia, and North Carolina, where voters—especially Hispanics—swung hard to Democrats. More moderate Republicans have urged the administration to adopt a quieter enforcement approach, focusing more narrowly on criminal offenders. Although the president has reportedly expressed concern to those close to him that some ICE tactics have gone too far, he has not ordered specific policy changes, according to three senior officials I spoke with at DHS. Those officials and others I’ve talked with told me they aren’t expecting a pullback, either. Trump’s decision to name Stephen Miller as his chief of staff yesterday places the chief architect and principal ideologue of the ICE campaign in charge of his administration. Miller’s promotion will give him even more power to mobilize other federal agencies to help ICE maximize deportations. Since Trump’s return to the White House, Republicans in Congress have given the administration nearly a quarter of a trillion dollars for the crackdown, aiming for 1 million deportations a year. ICE has obtained upwards of $110 billion, more than 11 times its annual budget, and the funding surge has created a powerful inertia. Absent a major policy reversal from Trump or a successful intervention by Democratic majorities in Congress—a long shot, experts say—Trump’s mass-deportation campaign will continue with its mandate to add more officers, more deportation flights, and more immigration jails. The campaign includes handing out wads of cash to local police and sheriff departments, which help the agency boost arrests. Prior to the midterms, ICE launched a hiring push to add 5,000 more employees—mostly deportation officers—by the end of the year. “Regardless of the political pressures that the White House may be feeling on immigration enforcement, the money creates a huge amount of momentum on its own,” Sarah Pierce, an immigration policy expert at the center-left think tank Third Way, told me. ICE has so much money that it will have to double its rate of spending to use it all before its deadline at the end of the 2029 fiscal year, she said. “Pulling that back would be extremely difficult for the White House.” [ Read: Losing the ‘big-ass truck’ vote ] Despite the midterm results, there hasn’t been a broad consensus in the Republican Party that overzealous ICE tactics were a vulnerability, and some right-wing commentators have pointed to exit-poll data showing that immigration was the top motivating issue for Republican voter turnout. At a polling place in the Dallas suburbs where I spoke with voters on Tuesday, several of the Republican supporters I met said they wanted Trump to stay the course. “Gotta keep locking it down,” said Danny, a 32-year-old hospital staffer I met outside a public library in Plano, north of Dallas. Danny told me he didn’t want his last name published, because he worried that he’d be harassed. His hometown and surrounding Collin County were reliably Republican when he was growing up, he said, but the region’s economic boom had brought in more transplants. “They keep voting for Democrats,” he said. “Democrats vote for more immigration. It’s a vicious cycle.” James Talarico, the Democratic winner of the Senate race in Texas, won Collin County by 12 points on Tuesday, a 23-point swing from Trump’s 2024 victory. It was the first time this century that Democrats have won statewide races in the county. Trump won nearly half the Hispanic vote nationwide in 2024, but this year Hispanics are estimated to have voted for Democrats by a 69–29 percent margin. C ould Democrats use their large majorities in Congress next year to force the administration to rein in ICE? Claire Trickler-McNulty, an attorney who has held several high-ranking roles at ICE, most recently during the Biden administration, told me that it will be hard for Democrats to change the trajectory of ICE spending. If Democrats pass an appropriations bill with language constraining or shifting ICE funds, Trump would have to sign it. “I don’t have a lot of confidence that he would sign that, but people I’ve talked to on the Hill feel like there may be a window or a path to a clawback, if you combine that with something he cares about,” Trickler-McNulty said. Trump has said he doesn’t want to spend the next two years “vetoing everything,” although the White House has also circulated a photo of a red VETO hat sitting on the Resolute Desk with the president in the background. Trump told Politico late Tuesday night that he’d be willing to work with Democrats on immigration reform if it were “appropriate and good for the country.” But the possibility of such negotiations could reduce the likelihood that Trump orders a different tack for ICE in the meantime. Mark Krikorian, the executive director of the Center for Immigration Studies, a leading immigration-restrictionist group, told me that the Trump administration has already shifted tactics, and could do so again. After the killings of two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis in January, Trump demoted Greg Bovino , the performative Border Patrol commander who was leading the crackdown in the city, and replaced Kristi Noem with Mullin, who said he wanted a more low-key ICE approach. That change marked the end of what Krikorian described as “theatricality,” generating ready-for-TV images of masked federal forces staging operations that thrilled the president’s base. But Krikorian said that an “imbalance” remains between “body-armor enforcement versus briefcase enforcement.” Trump could direct ICE to conduct more enforcement at worksites—not necessarily with raids that would send people running, Krikorian said, but with mundane audits that check Social Security numbers and other documents. “Worksite enforcement is something that has been very much lacking in this administration,” he said. It’s a lot less photogenic and a lot less politically tumultuous to just send in some bureaucrats.” [ Read: The secretary of homeland ] ICE continued to ramp up, with less fanfare, after Minneapolis , and the agency is now making more than 50,000 arrests a month, its highest rate ever. Officers have achieved those levels in part by using automated technologies, such as license-plate readers, and powerful database tools to make more traffic stops. Those public encounters deepened the backlash to ICE over the summer when officers shot several unarmed immigrants—two fatally—as they attempted to drive away. City and state governments have joined in that backlash, a trend that could accelerate with the widespread Democratic victories this week. The mayor of Houston announced yesterday that the city’s police will no longer contact ICE about nonviolent offenders who lack legal status. White-collar enforcement would not necessarily lead to arrests and deportations, but it would make it more likely for immigrants who are in the United States illegally to leave on their own, Krikorian said. The frustrations that Trump has been hearing from business owners may weigh against a crackdown on employers. Vice President Vance, who is considering running for president in 2028, appeared to signal a preference for that approach on Wednesday in a lengthy X post that assessed the party’s defeat. Vance wrote that he was “open” to shifting ICE’s focus to businesses that “hire illegal labor,” but said he didn’t support “amnesty,” the catch-all term used by immigration hard-liners who oppose creating a path to legal status for the estimated 12 million to 15 million immigrants who are illegally present in the United States. “Anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you,” Vance wrote. Pierce told me that she interpreted Vance’s post as a defense of the administration’s crackdown that was aimed at Republicans who view the midterm results as a rebuke. She said she’ll be watching to see if pressure on the administration to change tactics builds in the coming weeks or if the White House remains defensive and determined to follow the same course. [ Read: Repudiation ] There were also signs in Vance’s post of the conundrum that he and other potential Republican presidential candidates will likely face if they try to succeed Trump. Although there is broad support across the electorate for the deportation of immigrants who commit violent crimes or pose a threat to public safety, those immigrants represent only 10 to 20 percent of ICE arrests. Trump officials have spent the past two years appealing to the most ardent members of the MAGA movement, especially those who want DHS to be a tool of social and demographic transformation through the removal and “remigration” of millions of immigrants. Those views are too extreme for most voters in a general presidential election. But to win the party’s primaries, Vance, or any other potential Republican candidate, may need to embrace them. Ashley Parker and Michael Scherer contributed reporting.
